<!-- head-1: body_md -->
We use $\mathbb{N}$ for the type of natural numbers at the meta-level.
Contexts are snoc-lists written $\Gamma, x : T$.
Application of a substitution $\sigma$ to a term $t$ is written $t[\sigma]$, and
composition of substitutions is written $\sigma \circ \tau$ (meaning first $\sigma$, then $\tau$).
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:raw-exp}
  The set $\textsf{Exp}$ of raw expressions is generated by the following grammar:
  \[
    \begin{array}{rcll}
      t, s, S, T \in \textsf{Exp} & ::= & x & \text{(variable)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} & \text{(universe at level $i$)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} & \text{(natural number type)} \\
                          & \mid & \Pi(x : S).\, T & \text{(dependent function type, $x$ bound in $T$)} \\
                          & \mid & \textsf{zero} & \text{(zero)} \\
                          & \mid & \textsf{succ}~t & \text{(successor)} \\
                          & \mid & \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t} & \text{(natural number eliminator)} \\
                          & \mid & \lambda x.\, t & \text{(lambda abstraction, $x$ bound in $t$)} \\
                          & \mid & r~s & \text{(application)}
    \end{array}
  \]
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:ctx}
  Contexts $\Gamma, \Delta \in \textsf{Ctx}$ are ordered lists of variable-type pairs:
  \[
    \Gamma \in \textsf{Ctx} \quad ::= \quad \cdot \quad \mid \quad \Gamma, x : S
  \]
  where $\cdot$ is the empty context and $\Gamma, x : S$ extends $\Gamma$ with a fresh
  variable $x$ of type $S \in \textsf{Exp}$.
  We write $|\Gamma|$ for the length of $\Gamma$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:wk}
  A \emph{weakening} is a function $\phi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.
  The key operations on weakenings are:
  \begin{align*}
    \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) &= x \\
    {\Uparrow} &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & {\Uparrow}(x) &= x + 1 \\
    q(\phi) &: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} & q(\phi)(0) &= 0 \\
    && q(\phi)(x+1) &= \phi(x) + 1
  \end{align*}
  The shift $\Uparrow$ increments all indices by one (corresponding to introducing one new
  binding).
  The operation $q(\phi)$ extends a weakening under a binder: it fixes index~$0$
  (the newly bound variable) and applies $\phi$ followed by a successor to all
  other indices.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:wk-app}
  The application of a weakening $\phi$ to a term $t$, written $t[\phi]$, is
  defined by recursion on the structure of $t$:
  \begin{align*}
    x[\phi] &= \phi(x) \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} \\
    (\Pi(x : S).\, T)[\phi] &= \Pi(x : S[\phi]).\, (T[q(\phi)]) \\
    \textsf{zero}[\phi] &= \textsf{zero} \\
    (\textsf{succ}~t)[\phi] &= \textsf{succ}~(t[\phi]) \\
    (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t})[\phi] &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)])~z[\phi]~(x,y.\, s[q^2(\phi)])~t[\phi]} \\
    (\lambda x.\, t)[\phi] &= \lambda x.\, t[q(\phi)] \\
    (r\; s)[\phi] &= (r[\phi])\; (s[\phi])
  \end{align*}
  Whenever we pass under a binder, we extend the weakening with $q$.
  The successor case of the eliminator binds two variables ($x$ for the predecessor,
  $y$ for the inductive hypothesis), hence $q$ is applied twice.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-q-id}
  $q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By case analysis on the argument:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(0) &= 0 = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(0) \\
    q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(x+1) &= \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) + 1 = x + 1 = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x+1)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-id}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, $t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = t$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By induction on $t$.
  We show a few representative cases.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    \begin{align*}
      x[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \lambda x.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda x.\, t')[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})]) \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-q-id}} \\
      &= \lambda x.\, t'
        \tag{by IH}
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \Pi(x : S).\, T$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\Pi(x : S).\, T)[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]
      &= \Pi(x : S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]).\, (T[q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})]) \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, (T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])
        \tag{by IH and \Cref{lem:wk-q-id}} \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, T
        \tag{by IH}
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  All other cases follow the same pattern.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-q-comp}
  For all weakenings $\phi, \psi$:
  $q(\phi) \circ q(\psi) = q(\phi \circ \psi)$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By case analysis on the argument:
  \begin{align*}
    (q(\phi) \circ q(\psi))(0) &= q(\psi)(q(\phi)(0)) = q(\psi)(0) = 0 = q(\phi \circ \psi)(0)  \\
    (q(\phi) \circ q(\psi))(x+1) &= q(\psi)(\phi(x) + 1)
    = \psi(\phi(x)) + 1 \\
    &= (\phi \circ \psi)(x) + 1 = q(\phi \circ \psi)(x+1)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-qn-comp}
  For all weakenings $\phi, \psi$:
  $q^n(\phi) \circ q^n(\psi) = q^n(\phi \circ \psi)$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-comp}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$ and weakenings $\phi, \psi$:
  $t[\phi][\psi] = t[\phi \circ \psi]$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By induction on $t$.
  We show a few representative cases.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    \begin{align*}
      x[\phi][\psi] = (\phi(x))[\psi] = \psi(\phi(x)) = (\phi \circ \psi)(x) = x[\phi \circ \psi]
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \lambda x.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi][\psi]
      &= (\lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)]))[\psi] \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)][q(\psi)]) \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi) \circ q(\psi)])
        \tag{by IH} \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi \circ \psi)])
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-q-comp}} \\
      &= (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi \circ \psi]
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'}$.
    \begin{align*}
      & (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'})[\phi][\psi] \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)])~z[\phi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi)])~t'[\phi]})[\psi] \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi)][q(\psi)])~z[\phi][\psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi)][q^2(\psi)])~t'[\phi][\psi]} \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi) \circ q(\psi)])~z[\phi \circ \psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi) \circ q^2(\psi)])~t'[\phi \circ \psi]}
        \tag{by IH} \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\phi \circ \psi)])~z[\phi \circ \psi]~(x, y.\, s[q^2(\phi \circ \psi)])~t'[\phi \circ \psi]}
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-qn-comp}} \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t'})[\phi \circ \psi]
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  The cases for $\textsf{succ}~t$, $r\; s$, $\Pi$, $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$, $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$, and $\textsf{zero}$ are similar or
  immediate.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-cat}
  Weakenings satisfy:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem (Left identity) $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \phi = \phi$.
  \@idxitem (Right identity) $\phi \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} = \phi$.
  \@idxitem (Associativity) $(\phi \circ \psi) \circ \chi = \phi \circ (\psi \circ \chi)$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
All three are immediate from the definition of composition as function composition on $\mathbb{N}$:
  \begin{align*}
    (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \phi)(x) &= \phi(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x)) = \phi(x) \\
    (\phi \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(x) &= \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(\phi(x)) = \phi(x) \\
    ((\phi \circ \psi) \circ \chi)(x) &= \chi(\psi(\phi(x))) = (\phi \circ (\psi \circ \chi))(x)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:subst-ops}
  We define the following operations on substitutions:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \@idxitem \textbf{Identity.}
      $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} : \textsf{Subst}$, defined by $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x$.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Extension (cons).}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$, a variable $x$, and a term $s$, we write
      $(\sigma, s/x)$ for the substitution:
      \[
        (\sigma, s/x)(0) = s \qquad (\sigma, s/x)(x+1) = \sigma(x)
      \]
      Here $x$ is a visual mnemonic for the variable at de Bruijn index~0;
      under the hood, the extension always targets index~0.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Lifting under a binder.}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$, we define $q(\sigma) : \textsf{Subst}$ by:
      \[
        q(\sigma)(0) = 0 \qquad q(\sigma)(x+1) = (\sigma(x))[\Uparrow]
      \]
      This fixes index~0 and applies $\sigma$ to the remaining indices, weakening the
      results by one to account for the new binder.
    \@idxitem \textbf{Applying a weakening to a substitution.}
      Given a substitution $\sigma$ and a weakening $\phi$, we define
      $\sigma[\phi] : \textsf{Subst}$ pointwise:
      \[
        (\sigma[\phi])(x) = (\sigma(x))[\phi]
      \]
    \@idxitem \textbf{Composition.}
      Given substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$, their composition is:
      \[
        (\sigma \circ \tau)(x) = (\sigma(x))[\tau]
      \]
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:subst-app}
  The function $({-})[{-}] : \textsf{Exp} \to \textsf{Subst} \to \textsf{Exp}$ is defined by recursion on
  the structure of the expression:
  \begin{align*}
    x[\sigma] &= \sigma(x) \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \\
    \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma] &= \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} \\
    (\Pi(x : S).\, T)[\sigma] &= \Pi(x : S[\sigma]).\, (T[q(\sigma)]) \\
    \textsf{zero}[\sigma] &= \textsf{zero} \\
    (\textsf{succ}~t)[\sigma] &= \textsf{succ}~(t[\sigma]) \\
    (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x, y.\, s)~t})[\sigma] &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\sigma)])~z[\sigma]~(x,y.\, s[q^2(\sigma)])~t[\sigma]} \\
    (\lambda x.\, t)[\sigma] &= \lambda x.\, t[q(\sigma)] \\
    (r\; s)[\sigma] &= (r[\sigma])\; (s[\sigma])
  \end{align*}
  Whenever we pass under a binder, we lift $\sigma$ with $q$.
  The successor case of the eliminator binds two variables, hence $q$ is applied twice.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:wk-embed}
  Every weakening $\phi$ can be regarded as a substitution via the embedding:
  \[
    \iota(\phi) : \textsf{Subst} \qquad \iota(\phi)(x) = \phi(x)
  \]
  That is, $\iota(\phi)$ maps each index $n$ to the variable $\phi(x)$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-embed-correct}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$ and weakenings $\phi$:
  $t[\phi] = t[\iota(\phi)]$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By induction on $t$.
  The key observation is that $q(\iota(\phi)) = \iota(q(\phi))$:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\iota(\phi))(0) &= 0 = \iota(q(\phi))(0) \\
    q(\iota(\phi))(x+1) &= \iota(\phi)(x)[\Uparrow] = \phi(x)[\Uparrow] = \phi(x) + 1 = \iota(q(\phi))(x+1)
  \end{align*}
  With this fact, the induction is straightforward: at each binding form, we use
  $q(\iota(\phi)) = \iota(q(\phi))$ to relate the substitution side to the weakening side.
  For example:
  \begin{align*}
    (\lambda x.\, t')[\iota(\phi)]
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\iota(\phi))]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[\iota(q(\phi))]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\phi)])
      \tag{by IH} \\
    &= (\lambda x.\, t')[\phi]
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:iota-struct}
  The embedding $\iota$ preserves all weakening structure:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $\iota(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$.
  \@idxitem $\iota(\Uparrow) = \Uparrow$ (as substitutions, i.e.\ $\iota(\Uparrow)(x) = x + 1$).
  \@idxitem $\iota(q(\phi)) = q(\iota(\phi))$.
  \@idxitem $\iota(\phi \circ \psi) = \iota(\phi) \circ \iota(\psi)$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
$ $
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $\iota(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(x) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x)$.
  \@idxitem $\iota(\Uparrow)(x) = \Uparrow(x) = x + 1$.
    As a substitution, this is the variable $x+1$, which equals $\Uparrow$ viewed as a substitution.
  \@idxitem Already shown in the proof of \Cref{lem:wk-embed-correct}:
    $q(\iota(\phi))(0) = 0 = \iota(q(\phi))(0)$ and
    $q(\iota(\phi))(x+1) = \phi(x) + 1 = \iota(q(\phi))(x+1)$.
  \@idxitem We verify pointwise:
    \begin{align*}
      (\iota(\phi) \circ \iota(\psi))(x)
      &= \iota(\phi)(x)[\iota(\psi)] \\
      &= \phi(x)[\iota(\psi)] \\
      &= \psi(\phi(x))
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-embed-correct}} \\
      &= (\phi \circ \psi)(x) \\
      &= \iota(\phi \circ \psi)(x)
    \end{align*}
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-q-id}
  $q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By case analysis:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(0) &= 0 = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(0) \\
    q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(x+1) &= \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x)[\Uparrow] = x[\Uparrow] = x + 1 = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x+1)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-id}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$: $t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = t$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
By induction on $t$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    $x[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x$.
  \@idxitem $t = \lambda x.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda x.\, t')[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})]) \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-q-id}} \\
      &= \lambda x.\, t'
        \tag{by IH}
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \Pi(x:S).\, T$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\Pi(x:S).\, T)[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]
      &= \Pi(x : S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]).\, (T[q(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}})]) \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, (T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}])
        \tag{by IH and \Cref{lem:subst-q-id}} \\
      &= \Pi(x : S).\, T
        \tag{by IH}
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  All other cases are similar.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:qn-index}
  For all $n$ and weakenings $\phi$:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $x < n$, then $q^n(\phi)(x) = x$.
  \@idxitem $q^n(\phi)(x) = \phi(0) + x$.
  \@idxitem If $x > n$, then $q^n(\phi)(x) = \phi(x - n) + n$.
  \end{enumerate}
  In particular, for $\phi = \Uparrow$:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem[(a)] If $x < n$, then $q^n(\Uparrow)(x) = x$.
  \@idxitem[(b)] $q^n(\Uparrow)(x) = x + 1$.
  \@idxitem[(c)] If $x > n$, then $q^n(\Uparrow)(x) = x + 1$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By induction on $n$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $n = 0$: (1) vacuous. (2) $q^0(\phi)(0) = \phi(0) = \phi(0) + 0$.
    (3) $q^0(\phi)(x) = \phi(x) = \phi(x - 0) + 0$.
  \@idxitem $n + 1$: We use $q^{n+1}(\phi) = q(q^n(\phi))$.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \@idxitem If $x < n+1$: either $x = 0$ (then $q(q^n(\phi))(0) = 0 = x$) or
      $x = y + 1$ with $y < n$ (then $q(q^n(\phi))(y+1) = q^n(\phi)(y) + 1 = y + 1 = x$
      by the IH).
    \@idxitem $x = n + 1$: $q(q^n(\phi))(n+1) = q^n(\phi)(n) + 1 = (\phi(0) + n) + 1 = \phi(0) + (n+1)$
      by the IH.
    \@idxitem $x > n + 1$: $x = y + 1$ with $y > n$.
      $q(q^n(\phi))(y+1) = q^n(\phi)(y) + 1 = (\phi(y - n) + n) + 1 = \phi((y+1) - (n+1)) + (n+1)$
      by the IH.
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:qn-subst-index}
  For all $n$ and substitutions $\sigma$:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $x < n$, then $q^n(\sigma)(x) = x$.
  \@idxitem $q^n(\sigma)(n) = \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^n]$ (where $\Uparrow^n$ denotes $n$-fold shift).
  \@idxitem If $x > n$, then $q^n(\sigma)(x) = \sigma(x - n)[\Uparrow^n]$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By induction on $n$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $n = 0$: (1) vacuous. (2) $q^0(\sigma)(0) = \sigma(0) = \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^0]$.
    (3) $q^0(\sigma)(x) = \sigma(x) = \sigma(x-0)[\Uparrow^0]$.
  \@idxitem $n + 1$: We use $q^{n+1}(\sigma) = q(q^n(\sigma))$.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \@idxitem If $x < n+1$: either $x = 0$ (then $q(q^n(\sigma))(0) = 0 = x$) or
      $x = y + 1$ with $y < n$ (then $q(q^n(\sigma))(y+1) = (q^n(\sigma)(y))[\Uparrow] = y[\Uparrow] = y + 1 = x$
      by the IH (1)).
    \@idxitem $x = n + 1$:
      \begin{align*}
        q(q^n(\sigma))(n+1) &= (q^n(\sigma)(n))[\Uparrow] \\
        &= (\sigma(0)[\Uparrow^n])[\Uparrow]
          \tag{by IH (2)} \\
        &= \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}}
      \end{align*}
    \@idxitem $x > n+1$: $x = y + 1$ with $y > n$.
      \begin{align*}
        q(q^n(\sigma))(y+1) &= (q^n(\sigma)(y))[\Uparrow] \\
        &= (\sigma(y - n)[\Uparrow^n])[\Uparrow]
          \tag{by IH (3)} \\
        &= \sigma(y - n)[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}} \\
        &= \sigma((y+1) - (n+1))[\Uparrow^{n+1}]
      \end{align*}
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-subst-comm}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and substitutions $\sigma$:
  \[
    (t[q^n(\Uparrow)])[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] = t[q^n(\sigma)][q^n(\Uparrow)]
  \]
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
By induction on $t$, generalizing over $n$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    We must show $(q^n(\Uparrow)(x))[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] = (q^n(\sigma)(x))[q^n(\Uparrow)]$.
    We case-split on the position of $x$ relative to $n$.
    \begin{itemize}
    \@idxitem If $x < n$:
      \begin{align*}
        \text{LHS}
        &= (q^n(\Uparrow)(x))[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] \\
        &= x[q^{1+n}(\sigma)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-index}(a): $q^n(\Uparrow)(x) = x$ since $x < n$} \\
        &= x
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(1): $q^{1+n}(\sigma)(x) = x$ since $x < n < 1+n$}
      \end{align*}
      \begin{align*}
        \text{RHS}
        &= (q^n(\sigma)(x))[q^n(\Uparrow)] \\
        &= x[q^n(\Uparrow)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(1): $q^n(\sigma)(x) = x$ since $x < n$} \\
        &= x
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-index}(a)}
      \end{align*}

    \@idxitem If $x = n$:
      \begin{align*}
        \text{LHS}
        &= (q^n(\Uparrow)(n))[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] \\
        &= (n + 1)[q^{1+n}(\sigma)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-index}(b)} \\
        &= q^{1+n}(\sigma)(1+n) \\
        &= \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^{1+n}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(2) at iteration $1+n$}
      \end{align*}
      \begin{align*}
        \text{RHS}
        &= (q^n(\sigma)(n))[q^n(\Uparrow)] \\
        &= (\sigma(0)[\Uparrow^n])[q^n(\Uparrow)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(2)} \\
        &= \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^n \circ q^n(\Uparrow)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}} \\
        &= \sigma(0)[\Uparrow^{1+n}]
          \tag{since $(\Uparrow^n \circ q^n(\Uparrow))(x) = q^n(\Uparrow)(x + n) = x + 1 + n = \Uparrow^{1+n}(x)$}
      \end{align*}

    \@idxitem If $x > n$: Let $x = 1 + n + k$.
      \begin{align*}
        \text{LHS}
        &= (q^n(\Uparrow)(1 + n + k))[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] \\
        &= (2 + n + k)[q^{1+n}(\sigma)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-index}(c)} \\
        &= q^{1+n}(\sigma)(2 + n + k) \\
        &= \sigma(1+k)[\Uparrow^{1+n}]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(3): $(2+n+k) - (1+n) = 1+k$}
      \end{align*}
      \begin{align*}
        \text{RHS}
        &= (q^n(\sigma)(1 + n + k))[q^n(\Uparrow)] \\
        &= (\sigma(1+k)[\Uparrow^n])[q^n(\Uparrow)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:qn-subst-index}(3): $(1+n+k) - n = 1+k$} \\
        &= \sigma(1+k)[\Uparrow^n \circ q^n(\Uparrow)]
          \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-comp}} \\
        &= \sigma(1+k)[\Uparrow^{1+n}]
          \tag{as above}
      \end{align*}
    \end{itemize}

  \@idxitem $t = \lambda y.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda y.\, t')[q^n(\Uparrow)][q^{1+n}(\sigma)]
      &= (\lambda y.\, t'[q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)])[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] \\
      &= \lambda y.\, (t'[q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)][q^{2+n}(\sigma)]) \\
      &= \lambda y.\, (t'[q^{1+n}(\sigma)][q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)])
        \tag{by IH at $1+n$} \\
      &= (\lambda y.\, t'[q^{1+n}(\sigma)])[q^n(\Uparrow)] \\
      &= (\lambda y.\, t')[q^n(\sigma)][q^n(\Uparrow)]
    \end{align*}

  \@idxitem $t = \Pi(y : S).\, T$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\Pi(y:S).\,T)[q^n(\Uparrow)][q^{1+n}(\sigma)]
      &= (\Pi(y : S[q^n(\Uparrow)]).\, (T[q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)]))[q^{1+n}(\sigma)] \\
      &= \Pi(y : S[q^n(\Uparrow)][q^{1+n}(\sigma)]).\, (T[q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)][q^{2+n}(\sigma)]) \\
      &= \Pi(y : S[q^n(\sigma)][q^n(\Uparrow)]).\, (T[q^{1+n}(\sigma)][q^{1+n}(\Uparrow)])
        \tag{by IH at $n$ and $1+n$} \\
      &= (\Pi(y : S[q^n(\sigma)]).\, (T[q^{1+n}(\sigma)]))[q^n(\Uparrow)] \\
      &= (\Pi(y:S).\,T)[q^n(\sigma)][q^n(\Uparrow)]
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  The remaining cases follow the same pattern, applying the IH at increased $n$ for
  each binder.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-q-comp}
  For all substitutions $\sigma, \tau$:
  $q(\sigma) \circ q(\tau) = q(\sigma \circ \tau)$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By case analysis:
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem At index $0$:
    \begin{align*}
      (q(\sigma) \circ q(\tau))(0) = q(\sigma)(0)[q(\tau)] = 0[q(\tau)] = q(\tau)(0) = 0 = q(\sigma \circ \tau)(0)
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem At index $x+1$:
    \begin{align*}
      (q(\sigma) \circ q(\tau))(x+1)
      &= (q(\sigma)(x+1))[q(\tau)] \\
      &= (\sigma(x))[\Uparrow][q(\tau)] \\
      &= (\sigma(x))[\tau][\Uparrow]
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}} \\
      &= ((\sigma \circ \tau)(x))[\Uparrow] \\
      &= q(\sigma \circ \tau)(x+1)
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-assoc}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$ and substitutions $\sigma, \tau$:
  $t[\sigma][\tau] = t[\sigma \circ \tau]$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
By induction on $t$.
  \begin{itemize}[label=Case]
  \@idxitem $t = x$ (variable).
    $x[\sigma][\tau] = \sigma(x)[\tau] = (\sigma \circ \tau)(x) = x[\sigma \circ \tau]$.
  \@idxitem $t = \lambda x.\, t'$.
    \begin{align*}
      (\lambda x.\, t')[\sigma][\tau]
      &= (\lambda x.\, t'[q(\sigma)])[\tau] \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\sigma)][q(\tau)]) \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\sigma) \circ q(\tau)])
        \tag{by IH} \\
      &= \lambda x.\, (t'[q(\sigma \circ \tau)])
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-q-comp}} \\
      &= (\lambda x.\, t')[\sigma \circ \tau]
    \end{align*}
  \@idxitem $t = \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x,y.\,s)~t'}$.
    \begin{align*}
      &(\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x,y.\,s)~t'})[\sigma][\tau] \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\sigma)])~z[\sigma]~(x,y.\,s[q^2(\sigma)])~t'[\sigma]})[\tau] \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\sigma)][q(\tau)])~z[\sigma][\tau]~(x,y.\,s[q^2(\sigma)][q^2(\tau)])~t'[\sigma][\tau]} \\
      &= \ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T[q(\sigma \circ \tau)])~z[\sigma \circ \tau]~(x,y.\,s[q^2(\sigma \circ \tau)])~t'[\sigma \circ \tau]}
        \tag{by IH and \Cref{lem:subst-q-comp}} \\
      &= (\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x,y.\,s)~t'})[\sigma \circ \tau]
    \end{align*}
  \end{itemize}
  Other cases are similar.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:q-wk-comm}
  For all substitutions $\sigma$ and weakenings $\phi$:
  $q(\sigma[\phi]) = q(\sigma)[q(\phi)]$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Since $\sigma[\phi] = \sigma \circ \phi$ (treating $\phi$ as a substitution), we have:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\sigma[\phi])
    &= q(\sigma \circ \phi) \\
    &= q(\sigma) \circ q(\phi)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-q-comp}} \\
    &= q(\sigma)[q(\phi)]
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-subst-interact}
  The following two properties hold:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, weakening $\phi$, and substitution $\sigma$:
    $(t[\phi])[\sigma] = t[\phi \circ \sigma]$.
  \@idxitem For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, substitution $\sigma$, and weakening $\phi$:
    $(t[\sigma])[\phi] = t[\sigma[\phi]]$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Statement (1) is a corollary of \Cref{lem:wk-embed-correct,lem:subst-assoc}.
  Since we elide the embedding, treating $\phi$ as a substitution:
  \begin{align*}
    (t[\phi])[\sigma]
    &= t[\phi \circ \sigma]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}}
  \end{align*}

  Statement (2) also follows from \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}:
  \begin{align*}
    (t[\sigma])[\phi]
    &= t[\sigma \circ \phi]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}}
  \end{align*}
  We verify: $(\sigma \circ \phi)(x) = \sigma(x)[\phi] = (\sigma[\phi])(x)$,
  which is exactly the definition of $\sigma[\phi]$.
  Hence $\sigma \circ \phi = \sigma[\phi]$ and the claim holds.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:shift-ext}
  For all substitutions $\sigma$ and terms $s$:
  $\Uparrow \circ (\sigma, s/x) = \sigma$.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Pointwise:
  \begin{align*}
    (\Uparrow \circ (\sigma, s/x))(y)
    &= \Uparrow(y)[(\sigma, s/x)] \\
    &= (y+1)[(\sigma, s/x)] \\
    &= (\sigma, s/x)(y+1) \\
    &= \sigma(y)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:ext-comp}
  For all substitutions $\sigma, \tau$ and terms $s$:
  $(\sigma, s/x) \circ \tau = (\sigma \circ \tau,\; s[\tau]/x)$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Pointwise:
  \begin{align*}
    ((\sigma, s/x) \circ \tau)(0)
    &= (\sigma, s/x)(0)[\tau] \\
    &= s[\tau] \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \tau,\; s[\tau]/x)(0)
  \end{align*}
  \begin{align*}
    ((\sigma, s/x) \circ \tau)(y+1)
    &= (\sigma, s/x)(y+1)[\tau] \\
    &= \sigma(y)[\tau] \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \tau)(y) \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \tau,\; s[\tau]/x)(y+1)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:q-ext}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, substitutions $\sigma$, and terms $s$:
  \[
    t[q(\sigma)][\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x] = t[\sigma, s/x]
  \]
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}, it suffices to show $q(\sigma) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) = (\sigma, s/x)$.
  Recall $q(\sigma) = (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x)$.
  By \Cref{lem:ext-comp}:
  \begin{align*}
    q(\sigma) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow] \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x),\; 0[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)]/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= ((\sigma \circ \Uparrow) \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x),\; s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma \circ (\Uparrow \circ (\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x)),\; s/x)
       \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}},\; s/x) \tag{by \Cref{lem:shift-ext}} \\
    &= (\sigma, s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-id}}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:q-ext-gen}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, substitution $\sigma$, weakening $\phi$, and term $s$:
  \[
    t[q(\sigma)][\phi, s/x] = t[\sigma[\phi], s/x]
  \]
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}, it suffices to show
  $q(\sigma) \circ (\phi, s/x) = (\sigma[\phi], s/x)$.
  Recall $q(\sigma) = (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x)$.
  \begin{align*}
    q(\sigma) \circ (\phi, s/x)
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow], 0/x) \circ (\phi, s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma[\Uparrow] \circ (\phi, s/x),\; 0[(\phi, s/x)]/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= ((\sigma \circ \Uparrow) \circ (\phi, s/x),\; s/x) \\
    &= (\sigma \circ (\Uparrow \circ (\phi, s/x)),\; s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-cat} associativity} \\
    &= (\sigma \circ \phi,\; s/x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:shift-ext}} \\
    &= (\sigma[\phi],\; s/x)
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-cat}
  Substitutions satisfy:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem (Left identity) $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \sigma = \sigma$ for all $\sigma$.
  \@idxitem (Right identity) $\sigma \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} = \sigma$ for all $\sigma$.
  \@idxitem (Associativity) $(\sigma \circ \tau) \circ \delta = \sigma \circ (\tau \circ \delta)$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
$ $
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \sigma)(x) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x)[\sigma] = x[\sigma] = \sigma(x)$.
  \@idxitem $(\sigma \circ \ensuremath{\textsf{id}})(n) = \sigma(x)[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = \sigma(x)$ by \Cref{lem:subst-id}.
  \@idxitem By pointwise calculation:
    \begin{align*}
      ((\sigma \circ \tau) \circ \delta)(x)
      &= ((\sigma \circ \tau)(x))[\delta] \\
      &= (\sigma(x)[\tau])[\delta] \\
      &= \sigma(x)[\tau \circ \delta]
        \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}} \\
      &= (\sigma \circ (\tau \circ \delta))(x)
    \end{align*}
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-ext-comm}
  For all $t \in \textsf{Exp}$, substitutions $\sigma$, and terms $s$:
  \[
    t[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x] = t[s/x][\sigma]
  \]
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
We show both sides equal $t[\sigma, s[\sigma]/x]$.
  \begin{align*}
    t[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]
    &= t[q(\sigma)][\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by notation} \\
    &= t[\sigma, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:q-ext}}
  \end{align*}
  \begin{align*}
    t[s/x][\sigma]
    &= t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x][\sigma]
      \tag{by notation} \\
    &= t[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) \circ \sigma]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}} \\
    &= t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \sigma, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= t[\sigma, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-cat} (left identity)}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-ext-eta}
  For all substitutions $\sigma$:
  $\sigma = (\Uparrow \circ \sigma,\; x_0[\sigma]/x)$,
  where $x_0$ denotes the variable at index $0$.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Pointwise:
  \begin{align*}
    (\Uparrow \circ \sigma,\; x_0[\sigma]/x)(0)
    &= x_0[\sigma] = \sigma(0) \\
    (\Uparrow \circ \sigma,\; x_0[\sigma]/x)(y+1)
    &= (\Uparrow \circ \sigma)(y) \\
    &= \Uparrow(y)[\sigma] \\
    &= (y+1)[\sigma] \\
    &= \sigma(y+1)
  \end{align*}
  Hence both sides agree at every index.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{def:judgments}
  The judgments of our type theory are:
  \[
    \begin{array}{lll}
      \vdash \Gamma & & \text{$\Gamma$ is a well-formed context} \\[4pt]
      \typing[\Gamma]{t}{T} & & \text{$t$ has type $T$ in $\Gamma$} \\[4pt]
      \tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{T} & & \text{$t$ and $t'$ are equal terms of type $T$ in $\Gamma$} \\[4pt]
      
  \IfNoValueTF {S}
  {\Gamma \vdash T \subseteq &}
  {S \vdash T \subseteq &}
 & \text{$S$ is a subtype of $T$ in $\Gamma$}
    \end{array}
  \]
  Additionally, we have a derived judgment for substitution typing:
  \[
    \judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta} \qquad\qquad \text{$\sigma$ is a well-typed substitution from $\Delta$ to $\Gamma$}
  \]
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
$x_{|\Gamma|} : T[\Uparrow]^{1 + |\Gamma|} \in \Delta, x:T, \Gamma$
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-id-wt}
  If $\vdash \Gamma$, then $
  \wkjudge[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]{\Gamma : $}
.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We must show: for all $x : T \in \Gamma$, $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) : T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] \in \Gamma$.
  Since $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x$ and $T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = T$ (by \Cref{lem:wk-id}), this is immediate from
  $x : T \in \Gamma$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-shift-wt}
  If $\vdash \Gamma$ and $\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, then
  $\weakening[\Gamma, x_0 : S] \Uparrow \Gamma$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We must show: for all $y : T \in \Gamma$, $\Uparrow(y) : T[\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S$.
  We have $\Uparrow(y) = 1 + y$.
  From $y : T \in \Gamma$, the lookup rule gives $1{+}y : T[\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-q-wt}
  If $
  \wkjudge[\phi]{\Delta : $}
 and $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, then
  $\weakening[\Gamma, x_0 : S[\phi]] {q(\phi)} {\Delta, x_0 : S}$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
We must show: for all $y : T \in \Delta, x_0 : S$,
  $q(\phi)(y) : T[q(\phi)] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S[\phi]$.
  We case-split on the lookup $y : T \in \Delta, x_0 : S$:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $x_0 : S[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x_0 : S$:
    Then $q(\phi)(x_0) = x_0$ and
    $S[\Uparrow][q(\phi)] = S[\phi][\Uparrow]$ (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}).
    We have $x_0 : S[\phi][\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S[\phi]$ by lookup.
  \@idxitem $1{+}z : T'[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x_0 : S$ where $z : T' \in \Delta$:
    Then $q(\phi)(1{+}z) = 1{+}\phi(z)$ and
    $T'[\Uparrow][q(\phi)] = T'[\phi][\Uparrow]$ (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}).
    From $
  \wkjudge[\phi]{\Delta : $}
, we have $\phi(z) : T'[\phi] \in \Gamma$, so
    $1{+}\phi(z) : T'[\phi][\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S[\phi]$ by lookup.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-comp-wt}
  If $
  \wkjudge[\psi]{\Delta : $}
 and $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Theta$, then
  $
  \wkjudge[\phi \circ \psi]{\Theta : $}
.
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We must show: for all $x : T \in \Theta$,
  $(\phi \circ \psi)(x) : T[\phi \circ \psi] \in \Gamma$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\phi(x) : T[\phi] \in \Delta
      && \text{(from $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Theta$ and $x : T \in \Theta$)} \\
    &\psi(\phi(x)) : T[\phi][\psi] \in \Gamma
      && \text{(from $
  \wkjudge[\psi]{\Delta : $}
 and $\phi(x) : T[\phi] \in \Delta$)} \\
    &(\phi \circ \psi)(x) = \psi(\phi(x))
      && \text{(by definition of composition)} \\
    &T[\phi \circ \psi] = T[\phi][\psi]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-comp})}
  \end{align*}
  Hence $(\phi \circ \psi)(x) : T[\phi \circ \psi] \in \Gamma$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-typing}
  The following are proved by mutual induction on the syntactic judgments:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T}$ and $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Gamma$, then
    $\typing[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{T[\phi]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{T}$ and $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Gamma$, then
    $\tyequiv[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{t'[\phi]}{T[\phi]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\subty[\Gamma]{S}{T}$ and $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Gamma$, then
    $\subty[\Delta]{S[\phi]}{T[\phi]}$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By mutual induction on the derivation of the syntactic judgment.
  We show representative cases for statement (1).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Var}]
    {\vdash \Gamma \\ y : T \in \Gamma}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{y}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Then $y[\phi] = \phi(y)$.
  By the definition of $\weakening[\Delta] \phi \Gamma$, $\phi(y) : T[\phi] \in \Delta$.
  By \textsc{Var}, $\typing[\Delta]{\phi(y)}{T[\phi]}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\lambda$-I}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, y : S']{t}{T}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{\lambda y.\,t}{\Pi(y:S').\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\typing[\Delta]{(\lambda y.\,t)[\phi]}{(\Pi(y:S').\,T)[\phi]}$,
  i.e.\ $\typing[\Delta]{\lambda y.\,(t[q(\phi)])}{\Pi(y:S'[\phi]).\,(T[q(\phi)])}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\weakening[\Delta, y:S'[\phi]] {q(\phi)} {\Gamma, y:S'}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, y:S'[\phi]]{t[q(\phi)]}{T[q(\phi)]}
      && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{\lambda y.\,(t[q(\phi)])}{\Pi(y:S'[\phi]).\,(T[q(\phi)])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-I})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\lambda$-E}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, y:S']{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{r}{\Pi(y:S').\,T} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{s}{S'}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{r\;s}{T[s/y]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, y:S'[\phi]]{T[q(\phi)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{r[\phi]}{\Pi(y:S'[\phi]).\,(T[q(\phi)])} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{s[\phi]}{S'[\phi]} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{r[\phi]\;s[\phi]}{T[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/y]} && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-E})}
  \end{align*}
  It remains to show $T[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/y] = T[s/y][\phi]$,
  which is \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Subsump}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{t}{S} \\ \subty[\Gamma]{S}{T}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{T[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{S[\phi]} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\subty[\Delta]{S[\phi]}{T[\phi]} && \text{(by IH, statement (3))} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{T[\phi]} && \text{(by \textsc{Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  We now show representative cases for statement (2).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\beta$}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S']{t}{T'} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{s}{S'}}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,t)\;s}{t[s/x]}{T'[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\tyequiv[\Delta]{((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\phi]}{t[s/x][\phi]}{T'[s/x][\phi]}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\phi] = (\lambda x.\,(t[q(\phi)]))\;(s[\phi])
  \end{align*}
  Now:
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, x:S'[\phi]]{T'[q(\phi)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, x:S'[\phi]]{t[q(\phi)]}{T'[q(\phi)]}
      && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{s[\phi]}{S'[\phi]} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Delta]{(\lambda x.\,(t[q(\phi)]))\;(s[\phi])}{t[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/x]}{T'[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-$\beta$})}
  \end{align*}
  By \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm}:
  $t[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/x] = t[s/x][\phi]$ and $T'[q(\phi)][s[\phi]/x] = T'[s/x][\phi]$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\eta$}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{t}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\tyequiv[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\phi]}{(\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\phi]}$.
  Unfolding the right-hand side:
  \begin{align*}
    (\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\phi]
    &= \lambda x.\,((t[\Uparrow]\;x)[q(\phi)]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow][q(\phi)]\;x) \\
    &= \lambda x.\,(t[\phi][\Uparrow]\;x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}}
  \end{align*}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, x:S'[\phi]]{T'[q(\phi)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{\Pi(x:S'[\phi]).\,(T'[q(\phi)])} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\weakening[\Delta, x:S'[\phi]] \Uparrow \Delta
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-shift-wt})} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Delta]{t[\phi]}{\lambda x.\,(t[\phi][\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S'[\phi]).\,(T'[q(\phi)])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-$\eta$})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  We show a case for statement (3).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Sub-Pi}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \tyequiv[\Gamma]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \subty[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T'}}
    {\subty[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Delta]{S[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Delta]{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Delta]{S[\phi]}{S'[\phi]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH, statement (2))} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, x:S[\phi]]{T[q(\phi)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Delta, x:S'[\phi]]{T'[q(\phi)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\subty[\Delta, x:S[\phi]]{T[q(\phi)]}{T'[q(\phi)]}
      && \text{(by IH, statement (3), using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt})} \\
    &\subty[\Delta]{\Pi(x:S[\phi]).\,(T[q(\phi)])}{\Pi(x:S'[\phi]).\,(T'[q(\phi)])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Sub-Pi})}
  \end{align*}
  This is $\subty[\Delta]{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\phi]}{(\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\phi]}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  The remaining cases (\textsc{U-Wf}, \textsc{N-Wf}, \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf},
  \textsc{Ze-I}, \textsc{Su-I}, \textsc{N-E}, congruence rules,
  \textsc{Sub-Univ}, \textsc{Sub-Trans}, \textsc{Sub-Eq}) are analogous:
  apply the IH to each premise, using \Cref{lem:wk-q-wt} to construct
  the weakening for extended contexts, and re-apply the rule.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:id-wt}
  If $\vdash \Gamma$, then $\judge[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} : \Gamma}$.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We must show: for all $x : T \in \Gamma$, $\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x)}{T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]}$.
  Since $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}(x) = x$ and $T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = T$ (by \Cref{lem:subst-id}), this reduces to
  $\typing[\Gamma]{x}{T}$, which holds by \textsc{Var}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:ext-wt}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, and
  $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S[\sigma]}$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma]{(\sigma, s/x) : (\Delta, x : S)}$.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
We must show: for all $y : T \in \Delta, x : S$,
  $\typing[\Gamma]{(\sigma, s/x)(y)}{T[(\sigma, s/x)]}$.
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $x_0 : S[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x : S$:
    Then $(\sigma, s/x)(x_0) = s$ and
    $S[\Uparrow][(\sigma, s/x)] = S[\sigma]$ (by \Cref{lem:shift-ext,lem:subst-assoc}).
    We have $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S[\sigma]}$ by assumption.
  \@idxitem $1{+}z : T'[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x : S$ with $z : T' \in \Delta$:
    Then $(\sigma, s/x)(1{+}z) = \sigma(z)$ and
    $T'[\Uparrow][(\sigma, s/x)] = T'[\sigma]$ (by \Cref{lem:shift-ext,lem:subst-assoc}).
    From $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, $\typing[\Gamma]{\sigma(z)}{T'[\sigma]}$.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:single-subst-wt}
  If $\vdash \Gamma$, $\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, and $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S}$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma]{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) : (\Gamma, x : S)}$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:id-wt} and \Cref{lem:ext-wt}: $\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$ is well-typed by \Cref{lem:id-wt},
  and $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S} = \typing[\Gamma]{s}{S[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}]}$ by \Cref{lem:subst-id}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:wk-subst-wt}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$ and $\weakening[\Gamma'] \phi \Gamma$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma']{\sigma[\phi] : \Delta}$.
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
We must show: for all $x : T \in \Delta$,
  $\typing[\Gamma']{(\sigma[\phi])(x)}{T[\sigma[\phi]]}$.
  From $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, $\typing[\Gamma]{\sigma(x)}{T[\sigma]}$.
  By \Cref{lem:wk-typing}, $\typing[\Gamma']{\sigma(x)[\phi]}{T[\sigma][\phi]}$.
  Now $(\sigma[\phi])(x) = \sigma(x)[\phi]$ and $T[\sigma[\phi]] = T[\sigma][\phi]$
  (by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-interact}).
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:q-subst-typing}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, and
  $\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) : (\Delta, x_0 : S)}$.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
We must show that $q(\sigma)$ maps each variable in $(\Delta, x_0 : S)$ to a well-typed
  term in $(\Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma])$.
  We case-split on the lookup in $(\Delta, x_0 : S)$:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $x_0 : S[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x_0 : S$:
    \begin{align*}
      &q(\sigma)(x_0) = x_0 \\
      &S[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)] = S[\sigma][\Uparrow]
        && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm})} \\
      &x_0 : S[\sigma][\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma]
        && \text{(by lookup)}
    \end{align*}
    Hence $\typing[\Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma]]{x_0}{S[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)]}$ by \textsc{Var}.
  \@idxitem $1{+}y : T[\Uparrow] \in \Delta, x_0 : S$ where $y : T \in \Delta$:
    \begin{align*}
      &q(\sigma)(1{+}y) = \sigma(y)[\Uparrow] \\
      &\typing[\Gamma]{\sigma(y)}{T[\sigma]}
        && \text{(from $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$)} \\
      &\typing[\Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma]]{\sigma(y)[\Uparrow]}{T[\sigma][\Uparrow]}
        && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-typing} using \Cref{lem:wk-shift-wt})} \\
      &T[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)] = T[\sigma][\Uparrow]
        && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm})}
    \end{align*}
    Hence $\typing[\Gamma, x_0 : S[\sigma]]{\sigma(y)[\Uparrow]}{T[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)]}$.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-preserves}
  The following are proved by mutual induction on the syntactic judgments:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $\typing[\Delta]{t}{T}$ and $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, then
    $\typing[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$ and $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, then
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t'[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\subty[\Delta]{S}{T}$ and $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, then
    $
  \IfNoValueTF {S[\sigma]}
  {\Gamma \vdash T[\sigma] \subseteq $}
  {S[\sigma] \vdash T[\sigma] \subseteq $}
.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
By mutual induction on the derivation of the syntactic judgment.
  We show representative cases for statement (1).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\vdash \Delta \\ x : T \in \Delta}
    {\typing[\Delta]{x}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Then $t[\sigma] = x[\sigma] = \sigma(x)$.
  By the definition of $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, we have
  $\typing[\Gamma]{\sigma(x)}{T[\sigma]}$, which is the goal.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x : S]{t'}{T}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{\lambda x.\,t'}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\typing[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,t')[\sigma]}{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}$.
  Unfolding:
  \begin{align*}
    (\lambda x.\,t')[\sigma] &= \lambda x.\,(t'[q(\sigma)]) \\
    (\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] &= \Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])
  \end{align*}
  Now:
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) : (\Delta, x:S)} && \text{(by \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{t'[q(\sigma)]}{T[q(\sigma)]} && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\lambda x.\,(t'[q(\sigma)])}{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])} && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-I})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta]{r}{\Pi(x:S).\,T} \\ \typing[\Delta]{s}{S}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{r\;s}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\typing[\Gamma]{(r\;s)[\sigma]}{(T[s/x])[\sigma]}$.
  Unfolding: $(r\;s)[\sigma] = r[\sigma]\;s[\sigma]$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on second premise using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{r[\sigma]}{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
      && \text{(by IH on third premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{s[\sigma]}{S[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on fourth premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{r[\sigma]\;s[\sigma]}{T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-E})}
  \end{align*}
  It remains to show $T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x] = (T[s/x])[\sigma]$,
  which is \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta]{t}{S} \\ \subty[\Delta]{S}{T}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{t}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{S[\sigma]} && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &
  \IfNoValueTF {S[\sigma]}
  {\Gamma \vdash T[\sigma] \subseteq &}
  {S[\sigma] \vdash T[\sigma] \subseteq &}
& \text{(by IH, statement (3))} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]} && \text{(by \textsc{Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  The remaining cases (\textsc{U-Wf}, \textsc{N-Wf}, \textsc{Ze-I}, \textsc{Su-I})
  are straightforward applications of the IH.

  \medskip
  We now show representative cases for statement (2).
  The congruence cases follow directly from the IH.
  We show the computation and uniqueness rules.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S]{t}{T} \\ \typing[\Delta]{s}{S}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{(\lambda x.\,t)\;s}{t[s/x]}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\sigma]}{t[s/x][\sigma]}{T[s/x][\sigma]}$.
  Unfolding:
  \begin{align*}
    &((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\sigma] = (\lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma)]))\;(s[\sigma]) \\
    t[s/x][\sigma]
    &= t[(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}},s/x) \circ \sigma]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc}} \\
    &= t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \circ \sigma, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:ext-comp}} \\
    &= t[\sigma, s[\sigma]/x]
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:subst-cat} (left identity)}
  \end{align*}
  Now:
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{t[q(\sigma)]}{T[q(\sigma)]}
      && \text{(by IH using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{s[\sigma]}{S[\sigma]} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma)]))\;(s[\sigma])}{t[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]}{T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-$\beta$})}
  \end{align*}
  By \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm}:
  $t[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x] = (t[s/x])[\sigma]$ and
  $T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x] = (T[s/x])[\sigma]$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta]{t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma]}{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}$.
  Unfolding the right-hand side:
  \begin{align*}
    (\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma]
    &= \lambda x.\,((t[\Uparrow]\;x)[q(\sigma)]) \\
    &= \lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)]\;x) \\
    &= \lambda x.\,(t[\sigma][\Uparrow]\;x)
      \tag{by \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}}
  \end{align*}
  Now:
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{\lambda x.\,(t[\sigma][\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-$\eta$})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  We now show representative cases for statement (3).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\vdash \Delta \\ i \le j}
    {\subty[\Delta]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Then $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$ and $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}$.
  From $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, we have $\vdash \Gamma$.
  By \textsc{Sub-Univ}, $
  \IfNoValueTF {\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
  {\Gamma \vdash \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}} \subseteq $}
  {\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}} \vdash \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}} \subseteq $}
.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \tyequiv[\Delta]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \subty[\Delta, x:S]{T}{T'}}
    {\subty[\Delta]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{S'[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S'[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH, statement (2))} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S'[\sigma]]{T'[q(\sigma)]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &\subty[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{T'[q(\sigma)]}
      && \text{(by IH, statement (3), using \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing})} \\
    &
  \IfNoValueTF {\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
  {\Gamma \vdash \Pi(x:S'[\sigma]).\,(T'[q(\sigma)]) \subseteq &}
  {\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)]) \vdash \Pi(x:S'[\sigma]).\,(T'[q(\sigma)]) \subseteq &}
& \text{(by \textsc{Sub-Pi})}
  \end{align*}
  This is $
  \IfNoValueTF {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}
  {\Gamma \vdash (\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\sigma] \subseteq $}
  {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] \vdash (\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\sigma] \subseteq $}
.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Sub-Trans}: By two applications of the IH and \textsc{Sub-Trans}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Sub-Eq}: By statement (2) and \textsc{Sub-Eq}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-comp-wt}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$ and $\judge[\Gamma']{\tau : \Gamma}$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma']{\sigma \circ \tau : \Delta}$.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We must show: for all $x : T \in \Delta$,
  $\typing[\Gamma']{(\sigma \circ \tau)(x)}{T[\sigma \circ \tau]}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\sigma(x)}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(from $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma']{\sigma(x)[\tau]}{T[\sigma][\tau]}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves})} \\
    &(\sigma \circ \tau)(x) = \sigma(x)[\tau]
      && \text{(by definition)} \\
    &T[\sigma \circ \tau] = T[\sigma][\tau]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-assoc})}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:single-subst}
  If $\typing[\Gamma, x : S]{t}{T}$ and $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S}$, then
  $\typing[\Gamma]{t[s/x]}{T[s/x]}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:single-subst-wt} and \Cref{lem:subst-preserves}, noting
  $t[s/x] = t[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x]$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:presup}
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem If $\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T}$, then $\vdash \Gamma$ and $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$
    for some~$i$.
  \@idxitem If $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{T}$, then $\vdash \Gamma$,
    $\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T}$, $\typing[\Gamma]{t'}{T}$, and
    $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ for some~$i$.
  \@idxitem If $
  \IfNoValueTF {S}
  {\Gamma \vdash T \subseteq $}
  {S \vdash T \subseteq $}
, then $\vdash \Gamma$,
    $\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ and $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ for some $i$.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
By mutual induction on the derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\vdash \Gamma \\ x : T \in \Gamma}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{x}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We have $\vdash \Gamma$ immediately from the premise.
  For $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, we do induction on $x : T \in \Gamma$.
  If $\Gamma = \Gamma', x : T$, then $\vdash \Gamma', x : T$ was derived by
  \textsc{Ctx-Ext} from $\typing[\Gamma']{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$; weakening gives
  $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$.
  If $\Gamma = \Gamma', y : S$ and $x : T \in \Gamma'$, then by IH on the smaller
  context $\typing[\Gamma']{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$; weakening gives $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\vdash \Gamma}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We have $\vdash \Gamma$ from the premise.
  The type of the conclusion is $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}$, and $\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{2+i}}}$
  by another application of \textsc{U-Wf}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x : S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}} && \text{(by \textsc{U-Wf})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x : S]{t}{T}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{\lambda x.\,t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}} \text{ for some } j
      && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{\max(i,j)}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf} + \textsc{Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\\\ \typing[\Gamma]{r}{\Pi(x:S).\,T} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{s}{S}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{r\;s}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(directly from second premise)} \\
    &\judge[\Gamma]{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, s/x) : (\Gamma, x:S)} && \text{(by \Cref{lem:single-subst-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[s/x]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Gamma, x:\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{z}{T[\textsf{zero}/x]} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}, y:T]{s}{T[\Uparrow \circ \Uparrow, \textsf{succ}~x_1/x]} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{t}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\textsf{elim}_{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}~(x.\,T)~z~(x,y.\,s)~t}}{T[t/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on last premise)} \\
    &\judge[\Gamma]{(\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, t/x) : (\Gamma, x:\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}})} && \text{(by \Cref{lem:single-subst-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[t/x]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} on first premise)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{t}{S} \\ \subty{S}{T}}
    {\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} && \text{(directly from first premise)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Var-Cong}]
    {\vdash \Gamma \\ x : T \in \Gamma}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{x}{x}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We have $\vdash \Gamma$ from the premise.
  $\typing[\Gamma]{x}{T}$ by \textsc{Var}.
  $\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ by the same argument as the \textsc{Var} typing case above.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\beta$}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{t}{T} \\ \typing[\Gamma]{s}{S}}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,t)\;s}{t[s/x]}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,t)\;s}{T[s/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-E} on \textsc{$\lambda$-I})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t[s/x]}{T[s/x]}
      && \text{(by \Cref{cor:single-subst} on third premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[s/x]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \Cref{cor:single-subst} on second premise)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\eta$}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T} && \text{(directly from third premise)} \\
    &\weakening[\Gamma, x:S] \Uparrow \Gamma
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-shift-wt})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{t[\Uparrow]}{\Pi(x:S[\Uparrow]).\,(T[q(\Uparrow)])}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:wk-typing})} \\
    &x_0 : S[\Uparrow] \in \Gamma, x_0 : S
      && \text{(by lookup)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{x}{S[\Uparrow]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Var})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{t[\Uparrow]\;x}{T[q(\Uparrow)][x/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-E})} \\
    &T[q(\Uparrow)][x/x] = T[q(\Uparrow)][\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}, x/x] = T[\Uparrow, x/x]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:q-ext})} \\
    &(\Uparrow, x/x) = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-eta} at $\sigma = \ensuremath{\textsf{id}}$)} \\
    &T[\Uparrow, x/x] = T[\ensuremath{\textsf{id}}] = T
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-id})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma, x:S]{t[\Uparrow]\;x}{T}
      \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x)}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-I})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf} on first two premises)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Tm-Subsump}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{S} \\ \subty{S}{T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t}{t'}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t}{S} \text{ and } \typing[\Gamma]{t'}{S}
      && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{t}{T} \text{ and } \typing[\Gamma]{t'}{T}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Subsump} with third premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(directly from first premise)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Sub-Pi}]
    {\typing[\Gamma]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \tyequiv[\Gamma]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Gamma, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \subty[\Gamma, x:S]{T}{T'}}
    {\subty[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf} on premises 1 and 4)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf} on premises 2 and 5, using \textsc{Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Sub-Univ}]
    {\vdash \Gamma \\ i \le j}
    {\subty{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma && \text{(directly from premise)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Wf})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+j}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Wf})} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+j}}} \text{ and } \typing[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+j}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Subsump} with \textsc{Sub-Univ}, since $1+i \le 1+j$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  The remaining cases follow similar patterns.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{def:subst-equiv}
  $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$ holds when:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$ and
    $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma' : \Delta}$, and
  \@idxitem for every $x : T \in \Delta$,
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\sigma(x)}{\sigma'(x)}{T[\sigma]}$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:q-subst-equiv}
  If $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$ and
  $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$, then
  $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma') :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing}, $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$. We need $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma') :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$ as well: from
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$
  (by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2) applied to
  reflexivity on $\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$), the contexts
  $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]$ and $\Gamma, x:S[\sigma']$ are equivalent, so
  $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma') : (\Delta, x:S)}$ by
  \Cref{lem:q-subst-typing} and a context-conversion step.

  We verify clause~(2): for every $y : T \in \Delta, x:S$,
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma)(y)}{q(\sigma')(y)}
  {T[q(\sigma)]}$.
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $y = x_0$: $T = S[\Uparrow]$, $q(\sigma)(x_0) = x_0 =
    q(\sigma')(x_0)$. The required equality is reflexivity on $x_0$ at
    $S[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)] = S[\sigma][\Uparrow]$ (by
    \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}).
  \@idxitem $y = 1{+}z$ where $z : T' \in \Delta$:
    $q(\sigma)(1{+}z) = \sigma(z)[\Uparrow]$ and
    $q(\sigma')(1{+}z) = \sigma'(z)[\Uparrow]$. By clause~(2) of
    \Cref{def:subst-equiv} on $\sigma \approx \sigma'$,
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\sigma(z)}{\sigma'(z)}{T'[\sigma]}$. By
    \Cref{lem:wk-typing} applied to $\Uparrow$,
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]
      {\sigma(z)[\Uparrow]}{\sigma'(z)[\Uparrow]}
      {T'[\sigma][\Uparrow]}$,
    and $T'[\sigma][\Uparrow] = T'[\Uparrow][q(\sigma)]$ by
    \Cref{lem:wk-subst-comm}, which equals $T[q(\sigma)]$.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:subst-equiv-preserves}
  The following are proved by mutual induction on the syntactic
  judgments:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $\typing[\Delta]{t}{T}$ and
    $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$, then
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}$ and
    $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$, then
    $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t'[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}$.
  \@idxitem If $\subty[\Delta]{S}{T}$ and
    $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma \approx \sigma' : \Delta}$, then
    $\subty[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{T[\sigma']}$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
By mutual induction on the syntactic derivation, parallel to
  \Cref{lem:subst-preserves}. We show representative cases for
  statement~(1).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\vdash \Delta \\ x : T \in \Delta}
    {\typing[\Delta]{x}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Then $x[\sigma] = \sigma(x)$ and $x[\sigma'] = \sigma'(x)$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\sigma(x)}{\sigma'(x)}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by clause~(2) of \Cref{def:subst-equiv})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x : S]{t}{T}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{\lambda x.\,t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(\lambda x.\,t)[\sigma]}{(\lambda x.\,t)[\sigma']}
  {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}$.
  We first lift the equivalence under $q$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma') :
      (\Delta, x:S)}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:q-subst-equiv})} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{t[q(\sigma)]}{t[q(\sigma')]}
      {T[q(\sigma)]}
      && \text{(by IH on the second premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on the first premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma)])}
      {\lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma')])}
      {\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\lambda$-Cong})} \\
    &(\lambda x.\,t)[\sigma] = \lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma)]),\;
      (\lambda x.\,t)[\sigma'] = \lambda x.\,(t[q(\sigma')])
      && \text{(syntactic substitution)} \\
    &(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] = \Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])
      && \text{(syntactic substitution)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\\\
     \typing[\Delta]{r}{\Pi(x:S).\,T} \\ \typing[\Delta]{s}{S}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{r\;s}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(r\;s)[\sigma]}{(r\;s)[\sigma']}{T[s/x][\sigma]}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{r[\sigma]}{r[\sigma']}
      {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on the third premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s[\sigma]}{s[\sigma']}{S[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on the fourth premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{r[\sigma]\;s[\sigma]}{r[\sigma']\;s[\sigma']}
      {T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{App-Cong})} \\
    &(r\;s)[\sigma] = r[\sigma]\;s[\sigma],\;
      (r\;s)[\sigma'] = r[\sigma']\;s[\sigma']
      && \text{(syntactic substitution on application)} \\
    &T[q(\sigma)][s[\sigma]/x] = T[s/x][\sigma]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Wf}]
    {\vdash \Delta}
    {\typing[\Delta]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$ and $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma'] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\vdash \Gamma
      && \text{(from $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$ inside
        \Cref{def:subst-equiv})} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{1+i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Cong})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{N-Wf}: Analogous to \textsc{U-Wf}, with
  $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}} = \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma']$ and reflexivity by
  \textsc{N-Cong}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-Wf}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on first premise)} \\
    &\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma') :
      (\Delta, x:S)}
      && \text{(by lifting, as in the $\lambda$-I case)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{T[q(\sigma')]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
      {\Pi(x:S[\sigma']).\,(T[q(\sigma')])}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{$\Pi$-Cong})} \\
    &(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] = \Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])
      && \text{(syntactic substitution on $\Pi$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Ze-I}: $\textsf{zero}[\sigma] = \textsf{zero} = \textsf{zero}[\sigma']$;
  apply \textsc{Ze-Cong}. The type
  $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Su-I}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{t}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{\textsf{succ}~t}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}
      && \text{(by IH on premise; using $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{\textsf{succ}~t[\sigma]}{\textsf{succ}~t[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Su-Cong})} \\
    &(\textsf{succ}~t)[\sigma] = \textsf{succ}~t[\sigma],\;
      (\textsf{succ}~t)[\sigma'] = \textsf{succ}~t[\sigma']
      && \text{(syntactic substitution on $\textsf{succ}~$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{N-E}: analogous to \textsc{$\lambda$-E},
  applying the IH to each premise (motive, zero branch, step branch,
  scrutinee), lifting via $q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma')$ and
  $q^2(\sigma) \approx q^2(\sigma')$, and concluding by \textsc{N-E-Cong}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Subsump}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta]{t}{S} \\
     \subty[\Delta]{S}{T}}
    {\typing[\Delta]{t}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{S[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on second premise)} \\
    &\subty[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on third premise via statement~(3),} \\
    & && \text{instantiated at $\sigma \approx \sigma$, reflexive)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} on first premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Tm-Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  \textbf{Statement~(2): term-equality preservation.} By induction on
  the term-equality derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} (Congruence rules: \textsc{Var-Cong}, \textsc{U-Cong},
  \textsc{N-Cong}, \textsc{$\Pi$-Cong}, \textsc{Ze-Cong},
  \textsc{Su-Cong}, \textsc{$\lambda$-Cong}, \textsc{App-Cong},
  \textsc{N-E-Cong}). Each follows by IH on the premises and the same
  congruence rule, with substitution-on-syntax computed exactly as in
  statement~(1).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\beta$}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\ \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S]{t}{T} \\ \typing[\Delta]{s}{S}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{(\lambda x.\,t)\;s}{t[s/x]}{T[s/x]}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\sigma]}{t[s/x][\sigma']}
  {T[s/x][\sigma]}$.

  By \Cref{lem:q-subst-equiv} on $\sigma \approx \sigma'$ at $S$:
  $\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma') :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$. Apply IH statement~(1) to the third premise
  $\typing[\Delta, x:S]{t}{T}$ and to the fourth premise
  $\typing[\Delta]{s}{S}$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{t[q(\sigma)]}{t[q(\sigma')]}
      {T[q(\sigma)]}
      && \text{(by IH on third premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s[\sigma]}{s[\sigma']}{S[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on fourth premise)}
  \end{align*}
  Build the head-extended substitution equivalence:
  \begin{align*}
    &\judge[\Gamma]{(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x) \approx (\sigma', s[\sigma']/x)
      : (\Delta, x:S)}
      && \text{(at every $y \in \Delta$, both yield $\sigma(y),
        \sigma'(y)$,} \\
