    & && \text{equated by \Cref{def:subst-equiv} clause~(2) on
        $\sigma \approx \sigma'$;} \\
    & && \text{at $x$, the heads $s[\sigma], s[\sigma']$ are equated
        above)}
  \end{align*}
  Apply IH statement~(1) on the third premise
  $\typing[\Delta, x:S]{t}{T}$ at this equivalence:
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x)]}
      {t[(\sigma', s[\sigma']/x)]}
      {T[(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x)]}
      && \text{(by IH on third premise at the head-extended
        equivalence)} \\
    &t[s/x][\sigma] = t[(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x)]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm})} \\
    &t[s/x][\sigma'] = t[(\sigma', s[\sigma']/x)]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm})} \\
    &T[s/x][\sigma] = T[(\sigma, s[\sigma]/x)]
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-ext-comm})} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[s/x][\sigma]}{t[s/x][\sigma']}{T[s/x][\sigma]}
      && \text{(rewriting the previous equality line)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\sigma]}{t[s/x][\sigma]}
      {T[s/x][\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2) on the
        original $\beta$, at $\sigma$)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{((\lambda x.\,t)\;s)[\sigma]}{t[s/x][\sigma']}
      {T[s/x][\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Tm-Trans})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$\Pi$-$\eta$}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta]{t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x)}
      {\Pi(x:S).\,T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  We must show
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma']}
  {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}$.

  By IH statement~(1) on the third premise:
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on $\typing[\Delta]{t}{\Pi(x:S).\,T}$)}
  \end{align*}
  Apply \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2) on the original
  $\eta$-rule at $\sigma'$ (a well-typed substitution since
  $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma' : \Delta}$ by \Cref{def:subst-equiv} clause~(1)):
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma']}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma']}
      {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma']}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2)
        on $\eta$ at $\sigma'$)}
  \end{align*}
  Bridge the type from $\sigma'$ to $\sigma$ via the $\Pi$-Wf case of
  statement~(1), already proved on
  $\typing[\Delta]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ (derivable from the first two
  $\eta$-premises by \textsc{$\Pi$-Wf}):
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}{(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma']}
      {\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by the $\Pi$-Wf case of statement~(1))} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma']}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma']}
      {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Tm-Subsump} with \textsc{Sub-Eq})} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{(\lambda x.\,(t[\Uparrow]\;x))[\sigma']}
      {(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Tm-Trans})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{N-$\beta$-ze}, \textsc{N-$\beta$-su}: analogous
  to $\beta$ above. Apply \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2) to
  the original reduction rule at $\sigma$ to get equality at the
  contractum-substituted-by-$\sigma$. Then apply IH (statement~(1)) to
  the typing of the contractum (derivable from the reduction rule and
  \Cref{lem:presup}) to bridge the contractum from $\sigma$ to
  $\sigma'$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Tm-Sym}]
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t'}{t}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  By IH on the premise (with the roles of $\sigma, \sigma'$ swapped):
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma']}{t'[\sigma]}{T[\sigma']}$. By
  \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} statement~(2), $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{T[\sigma]}
  {T[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$ (from the reflexive closure on the
  type-formation of $T$ via presupposition). By \textsc{Tm-Subsump}
  with \textsc{Sub-Eq}, transport to the goal type $T[\sigma]$:
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t'[\sigma]}{t[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}$, then apply
  \textsc{Tm-Sym}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Tm-Trans}]
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T} \\\\ \tyequiv[\Delta]{t'}{t''}{T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t''}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  By IH on the first premise:
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t'[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]}$ (instantiated at
  $\sigma \approx \sigma$, reflexive). By IH on the second premise:
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t'[\sigma]}{t''[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}$. By
  \textsc{Tm-Trans}: $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t''[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Tm-Subsump}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\\\
     \tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{S} \\
     \subty[\Delta]{S}{T}}
    {\tyequiv[\Delta]{t}{t'}{T}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t'[\sigma']}{S[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on the second premise)} \\
    &\subty[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by IH on the third premise via statement~(3),
        instantiated} \\
    & && \text{at $\sigma \approx \sigma$, reflexive)} \\
    &\typing[\Gamma]{T[\sigma]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subst-preserves} on the first premise)} \\
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{t[\sigma]}{t'[\sigma']}{T[\sigma]}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Tm-Subsump})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  \textbf{Statement~(3): subtyping preservation.} By induction on the
  subtyping derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Sub-Univ}: $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}[\sigma] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}$,
  $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}[\sigma'] = \ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}$, and the conclusion follows from
  \textsc{Sub-Univ} at $i \le j$ (the same hypothesis), with $\vdash
  \Gamma$ from $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Sub-Pi}]
    {\typing[\Delta]{S}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta]{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \tyequiv[\Delta]{S}{S'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\\\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \typing[\Delta, x:S']{T'}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}} \\
     \subty[\Delta, x:S]{T}{T'}}
    {\subty[\Delta]{\Pi(x:S).\,T}{\Pi(x:S').\,T'}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &\tyequiv[\Gamma]{S[\sigma]}{S'[\sigma']}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}
      && \text{(by IH on third premise, statement~(2))} \\
    &\judge[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{q(\sigma) \approx q(\sigma') :
      (\Delta, x:S)}
      && \text{(by lifting)} \\
    &\subty[\Gamma, x:S[\sigma]]{T[q(\sigma)]}{T'[q(\sigma')]}
      && \text{(by IH on sixth premise)} \\
    &\subty[\Gamma]{\Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])}
      {\Pi(x:S'[\sigma']).\,(T'[q(\sigma')])}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Sub-Pi} on the previous lines and IH on
        the well-formedness} \\
    & && \text{premises 1, 2, 4, 5)} \\
    &(\Pi(x:S).\,T)[\sigma] = \Pi(x:S[\sigma]).\,(T[q(\sigma)])
      && \text{(syntactic)} \\
    &(\Pi(x:S').\,T')[\sigma'] = \Pi(x:S'[\sigma']).\,(T'[q(\sigma')])
      && \text{(syntactic)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Sub-Trans}: by IH on both premises and
  \textsc{Sub-Trans}, using a shared middle subtype evaluated at
  $\sigma$ on both sides.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Sub-Eq}: by IH on the premise via statement~(2)
  and \textsc{Sub-Eq}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:subst-head-eq}
  If $\typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$,
  $\judge[\Gamma]{\sigma : \Delta}$, and
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s}{s'}{S[\sigma]}$, then
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{T[\sigma, s/x]}{T[\sigma, s'/x]}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
By \Cref{lem:presup}, $\typing[\Gamma]{s}{S[\sigma]}$ and
  $\typing[\Gamma]{s'}{S[\sigma]}$ from
  $\tyequiv[\Gamma]{s}{s'}{S[\sigma]}$.
  Build the substitution equivalence
  $\judge[\Gamma]{(\sigma, s/x) \approx (\sigma, s'/x) :
    (\Delta, x:S)}$: at every $y \in \Delta$ both sides yield
  $\sigma(y)$, and at $x$ the heads $s, s'$ are equated at $S[\sigma]$
  by hypothesis. Apply \Cref{lem:subst-equiv-preserves} statement~(1)
  to $\typing[\Delta, x:S]{T}{\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{i}}}$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{def:domain}
  The domain $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}$, neutral values $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n$, normal forms $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_f$, and
  environments $\textsf{Env}$ are defined mutually as follows:
  \[
    \begin{array}{rrcl}
      \textit{Environments} & \rho & \in & \textsf{Env} = \mathbb{N} \to \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}} \\[6pt]
      \textit{Domain values} & a, b, A, B & \in & \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}} \\
      & & ::= & U_i \mid N \mid \Pi(a, t, \rho) \mid \texttt{ze} \mid \texttt{su}(a)
                \mid \lambda(t, \rho) \mid {\uparrow^A(e)} \\[6pt]
      \textit{Neutral values} & e & \in & \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n \\
      & & ::= & \ell_n \mid e \; \$ \; d
                \mid \mathsf{rec}(T, a, s, \rho, e) \\[6pt]
      \textit{Normal forms} & d & \in & \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_f \\
      & & ::= & {\downarrow}^A(a)
    \end{array}
  \]
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
The follow evaluations hold:
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem $\ensuremath{\llbracket \iota(\psi) \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow \ensuremath{\llbracket \psi \rrbracket(\rho)}$
  \@idxitem $\ensuremath{\llbracket \ensuremath{\textsf{id}} \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow \rho$,
  \@idxitem If $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow \rho'$ and $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a$, then
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket \sigma, t/x \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow (\rho', a)$. 
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{lem:det}
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem If $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a$ and $\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\rho)} \searrow a'$, then $a = a'$.
  \@idxitem If $f \cdot a \searrow b$ and $f \cdot a \searrow b'$, then $b = b'$.
  \@idxitem If $\mathsf{rec}(a, T, z, s, \rho) \searrow b$ and
    $\mathsf{rec}(a, T, z, s, \rho) \searrow b'$, then $b = b'$.
  \@idxitem If $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n(d) \searrow w$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n(d) \searrow w'$,
    then $w = w'$.
  \@idxitem If $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}_n(A) \searrow W$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}_n(A) \searrow W'$,
    then $W = W'$.
  \@idxitem If $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u'$,
    then $u = u'$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
By mutual induction on the derivations.
  In each case, the conclusion follows because the rules are syntax-directed: no two
  rules apply to the same configuration.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{def:init-env}
  Given a context $\Gamma$, the initial environment
  ${\uparrow}^\Gamma : \textsf{Env}$ is defined by induction on $\Gamma$:
  \[
    \begin{array}{lcl}
      {\uparrow}^{\cdot}(x) & = & \texttt{ze} \\[4pt]
      {\uparrow}^{\Gamma, x : T} & = &
        ({\uparrow}^\Gamma,\; {\uparrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket({\uparrow}^\Gamma)}}(\ell_{|\Gamma|}))
    \end{array}
  \]
  Each variable $x_i$ in $\Gamma$ is mapped to a neutral value ${\uparrow}^{A_i}(\ell_i)$
  reflecting $x_i$ at its evaluated type $A_i$.
  Here $|\Gamma|$ denotes the length of $\Gamma$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
\label{def:nbe}
  Given $
  \judge[t]{T : $}
, we define
  \[
    \textsf{nbe}^T_\Gamma(t) := \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_{|\Gamma|}({\downarrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\uparrow^\Gamma)}}(\ensuremath{\llbracket t \rrbracket(\uparrow^\Gamma)}))
  \]
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:per-nf}
  Two annotated normal forms $d, d' \in \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_f$ are related in $\textsf{Nf}$ if they read back to
  the same syntactic normal form at every name supply level:
  \[
    d \approx d' \in \textsf{Nf}
    \;:=\;
    \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \exists\, w.\;
    \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n(d) \searrow w \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n(d') \searrow w
  \]
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{def:per-ne}
  Two neutral domain values $e, e'$ are related in $\textsf{Ne}$ if they read back to the same
  neutral normal form at every name supply level:
  \[
    e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
    \;:=\;
    \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \exists\, u.\;
    \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u
  \]
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{def:per-ty}
  Two domain values $A, A'$ representing types are related in $\textsf{Ty}$ if they
  read back to the same type normal form:
  \[
    A \approx A' \in \textsf{Ty}
    \;:=\;
    \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \exists\, W.\;
    \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}_n(A) \searrow W
    \;\wedge\;
    \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}_n(A') \searrow W
  \]
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
\label{lem:base-per}
  $\textsf{Nf}$, $\textsf{Ne}$, and $\textsf{Ty}$ are symmetric and transitive (hence PERs).
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Symmetry is immediate (swap the two conjuncts).
  Transitivity follows from determinism of readback (\Cref{lem:det}).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsf{Ne}$.
  Suppose $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$ and $e' \approx e'' \in \textsf{Ne}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, u.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u
      && \text{(by first hypothesis)} \\
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, u'.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u' \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e'') \searrow u'
      && \text{(by second hypothesis)} \\
    &u = u'
      && \text{(by determinism of $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}$, \Cref{lem:det})} \\
    &\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e'') \searrow u
      && \text{(combining above)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  The cases for $\textsf{Nf}$ and $\textsf{Ty}$ are analogous, using determinism of
  $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}$ and $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ty}}$ respectively.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{def:per-neu}
  \[
    {\uparrow}^A(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(e') \in \textsf{Neu}
    \;:=\;
    e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
  \]
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{def:per-nat}
  The relation $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$ is defined inductively by:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ze}]
    { }
    {\texttt{ze} \approx \texttt{ze} \in \textsf{Nat}}
    ; \gdef, {, }
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Su}]
    {a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}}
    {\texttt{su}(a) \approx \texttt{su}(a') \in \textsf{Nat}}
    ; \gdef, {, }
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ne}]
    {e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^N(e) \approx {\uparrow}^N(e') \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
\label{lem:nat-per}
  $\textsf{Nat}$ is symmetric and transitive.
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ze}]
    { }
    {\texttt{ze} \approx \texttt{ze} \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Symmetry and transitivity are immediate.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Su}]
    {a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}}
    {\texttt{su}(a) \approx \texttt{su}(a') \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &a' \approx a \in \textsf{Nat}
      && \text{(by IH, symmetry)} \\
    &\texttt{su}(a') \approx \texttt{su}(a) \in \textsf{Nat}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Nat-Su})}
  \end{align*}
  Transitivity: given additionally $\texttt{su}(a') \approx \texttt{su}(a'') \in \textsf{Nat}$
  (hence $a' \approx a'' \in \textsf{Nat}$), by the IH $a \approx a'' \in \textsf{Nat}$,
  so $\texttt{su}(a) \approx \texttt{su}(a'') \in \textsf{Nat}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ne}]
    {e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^N(e) \approx {\uparrow}^N(e') \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &e' \approx e \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by symmetry of $\textsf{Ne}$, \Cref{lem:base-per})} \\
    &{\uparrow}^N(e') \approx {\uparrow}^N(e) \in \textsf{Nat}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Nat-Ne})}
  \end{align*}
  Transitivity follows analogously from transitivity of $\textsf{Ne}$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{lem:nat-readback}
  If $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$, then
  ${\downarrow}^N(a) \approx {\downarrow}^N(a') \in \textsf{Nf}$.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation of $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ze}]
    { }
    {\texttt{ze} \approx \texttt{ze} \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both sides read back to $\textsf{zero}$ at every level $n$, so
  ${\downarrow}^N(\texttt{ze}) \approx {\downarrow}^N(\texttt{ze}) \in \textsf{Nf}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Su}]
    {a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}}
    {\texttt{su}(a) \approx \texttt{su}(a') \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &{\downarrow}^N(a) \approx {\downarrow}^N(a') \in \textsf{Nf}
      && \text{(by IH)} \\
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, w.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N(a)) \searrow w \;\wedge\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N(a')) \searrow w
      && \text{(by definition of $\textsf{Nf}$)} \\
    &\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N(\texttt{su}(a))) \searrow \textsf{succ}~w \;\wedge\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N(\texttt{su}(a'))) \searrow \textsf{succ}~w
      && \text{(by \textsc{Rf-su})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Nat-Ne}]
    {e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^N(e) \approx {\uparrow}^N(e') \in \textsf{Nat}}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by hypothesis)} \\
    &\forall\, n.\; \exists\, u.\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e) \searrow u \;\wedge\; \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Ne}}_n(e') \searrow u
      && \text{(by definition of $\textsf{Ne}$)} \\
    &\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N({\uparrow}^N(e))) \searrow u \;\wedge\;
      \textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^N({\uparrow}^N(e'))) \searrow u
      && \text{(by \textsc{Rf-ne})}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{def:per-univ}
  The relation $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$ is defined inductively by the following
  four cases.
  The returned $R$ is unique only up to $\Leftrightarrow$ (not definitional equality).
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i
      \searrow R}

    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Univ}]
    {j < i \\ R \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_j}
    {U_j \approx U_j \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}

    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Nat}]
    {R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}}
    {N \approx N \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}

    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  In the $\textsc{U-Pi}$ case, $\Pi(A, T, \rho)$ is the closure form: the codomain
  fiber at input $b$ is obtained by evaluating $T$ in $(\rho, b/x)$.
  The notation $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$ means that $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ is the proof/evidence
  that $a \approx a' \in R_I$ holds; $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ may depend on this evidence.
  The fourth premise characterizes $R$ as the PER on functions: $f, f'$ are
  related in $R$ if and only if applying them to related inputs yields related outputs.
  We write $f \cdot a$ for semantic application (i.e., there exists $c$ with
  $f \cdot a \searrow c$, and $c$ participates in $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$).
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Several points deserve emphasis:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem The returned $R$ in each case is specified only up to $\Leftrightarrow$.
    This makes $\mathcal{U}_i$ a \emph{weak} partial functional relation, avoiding the need
    for propositional or functional extensionality.
  \@idxitem The premise ``$R_I$ is a PER'' in $\textsc{U-Pi}$ strengthens the
    induction principle: it allows proving that returned PERs are PERs without
    extra axioms.
    Once symmetry and transitivity of the returned PER are established
    (see below), the premise becomes logically
    redundant but is needed for the induction to go through.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{lem:cumul}
  If $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$ and $i \le j$, then
  $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R$.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation of $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  The same derivation works at level $j$ (neutrals are level-independent):
  ${\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R$ by \textsc{U-Ne}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Univ}]
    {k < i \\ R \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_k}
    {U_k \approx U_k \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &k < i \le j
      && \text{(by hypothesis)} \\
    &U_k \approx U_k \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Univ}, since $k < j$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Nat}]
    {R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}}
    {N \approx N \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  Level-independent: $N \approx N \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R$ by \textsc{U-Nat}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_I
      && \text{(by IH on domain)} \\
    &\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by IH on codomain)} \\
    &\Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Pi})}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{def:sem-subty}
  The relation $A \mathrel{<:_i} A'$ is defined inductively by:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \mathrel{<:_i} {\uparrow}^{A'}(b')}

    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Univ}]
    {j \le k \\ k < i}
    {U_j \mathrel{<:_i} U_k}

    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Nat}]
    { }
    {N \mathrel{<:_i} N}

    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \\\\
     \Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A, T, \rho) \in \mathcal{U}_i \\
     \Pi(A', T', \rho') \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \mathrel{<:_i} \Pi(A', T', \rho')}
  \end{mathpar}
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{lem:univ-functional}
  If $A \approx B \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$ and $A \approx B' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R'$,
  then $R \Leftrightarrow R'$.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
By induction on the two derivations simultaneously.
  The cases are forced: $N$ can only match $\textsc{U-Nat}$, a neutral can only match
  $\textsc{U-Ne}$, etc.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Ne}$.
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both derivations force $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$ and
  $R' \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$, so $R \Leftrightarrow R'$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Nat}$.
  Both derivations force $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}$ and
  $R' \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}$, so $R \Leftrightarrow R'$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Univ}$.
  Both derivations force $R \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_j$ and
  $R' \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_j$, so $R \Leftrightarrow R'$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Pi}$.
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  From the second derivation we get $R_I'$ with
  $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I'$.
  \begin{align*}
    &R_I \Leftrightarrow R_I'
      && \text{(by IH on domain)} \\
    &\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
      R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by IH on codomain at each input)} \\
    &R \Leftrightarrow R'
      && \text{(by the biconditional characterizations and transitivity of $\Leftrightarrow$)}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{lem:univ-sym}
  If $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, then:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $A' \approx A \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, and
  \@idxitem $a \approx a' \in R$ implies $a' \approx a \in R$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation.  We prove both statements simultaneously.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1):
  \begin{align*}
    &b' \approx b \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by symmetry of $\textsf{Ne}$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \approx {\uparrow}^A(b) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Ne})}
  \end{align*}
  For (2): Suppose $a \approx a' \in R$, i.e.\ $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Neu}$
  (since $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$).
  Then $a = {\uparrow}^B(e)$ and $a' = {\uparrow}^{B'}(e')$ with $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$.
  By symmetry of $\textsf{Ne}$, $e' \approx e \in \textsf{Ne}$, so $a' \approx a \in \textsf{Neu}$,
  i.e.\ $a' \approx a \in R$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Univ}]
    {j < i \\ R \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_j}
    {U_j \approx U_j \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): Immediate ($U_j \approx U_j$ is symmetric).

  For (2): Suppose $a \approx a' \in R$, i.e.\ $a \approx a' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_0$
  for some $R_0$.
  By the IH at level $j$ (which is structurally smaller), $a' \approx a \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_0$,
  so $a' \approx a \in R$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Nat}]
    {R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}}
    {N \approx N \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): Immediate.

  For (2): Suppose $a \approx a' \in R$, i.e.\ $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$.
  By symmetry of $\textsf{Nat}$ (\Cref{lem:nat-per}), $a' \approx a \in \textsf{Nat}$,
  so $a' \approx a \in R$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): We construct a \textsc{U-Pi} derivation of
  $\Pi(A', T', \rho') \approx \Pi(A, T, \rho) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.
  We verify the four premises.

  \emph{Premise 1} (domain):
  \begin{align*}
    &A' \approx A \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I
      && \text{(by IH (1) on domain; same $R_I$ by \Cref{lem:univ-functional})}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Premise 2}: $R_I$ is a PER (by hypothesis).

  \emph{Premise 3} (codomain): Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a' \approx a \in R_I$.
  \begin{align*}
    &a \approx a' \in R_I
      && \text{(by symmetry of $R_I$; call this $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)
      && \text{(original codomain premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)
      && \text{(by IH (1) on codomain; same $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)$ returned)}
  \end{align*}
  Define $R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') := R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)$.

  \emph{Premise 4} (biconditional): We must show
  \[
    \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
    (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a' \approx a \in R_I.\; f \cdot a' \approx f' \cdot a \in R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'))
  \]
  Since $R_I$ is a PER, the set of pairs $\{(a, a') \mid a \approx a' \in R_I\}$ is
  closed under swapping: $(a, a') \in R_I$ iff $(a', a) \in R_I$.
  By right irrelevance (\Cref{lem:univ-functional}), $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ depends only on the pair
  $(a, a')$, not the specific evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$.
  Hence the right-hand side
  ``$\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a' \approx a \in R_I.\; f \cdot a' \approx f' \cdot a \in R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$''
  is, after renaming bound variables $(a' \mapsto b, a \mapsto b')$, equivalent to
  ``$\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'':: b \approx b' \in R_I.\; f \cdot b \approx f' \cdot b' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'')$''
  which is exactly the original right-hand side.
  Therefore the same $R$ satisfies both biconditionals.
  \begin{align*}
    &\Pi(A', T', \rho') \approx \Pi(A, T, \rho) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Pi})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  For (2): Suppose $f \approx f' \in R$.
  We must show $f' \approx f \in R$, i.e.\ for all $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$,
  $f' \cdot a \approx f \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &a' \approx a \in R_I
      && \text{(by symmetry of $R_I$)} \\
    &\text{let } \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a' \approx a \in R_I \\
    &f \cdot a' \approx f' \cdot a \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(from $f \approx f' \in R$, applied to $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}: both have same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)}$)} \\
    &f' \cdot a \approx f \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by IH (2) on $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$)} \\
    &f' \cdot a \approx f \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$)}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{lem:univ-trans}
  If $A_1 \approx A_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, then:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $A_2 \approx A_3 \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R'$ implies
    $A_1 \approx A_3 \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, and
  \@idxitem $a_1 \approx a_2 \in R$ and $a_2 \approx a_3 \in R$ implies
    $a_1 \approx a_3 \in R$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
By induction on the two derivations.
  We must case-split on both; by the structure of the definition, matching cases are forced
  (e.g., $N$ can only relate to $N$).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Ne}$.
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  and
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b' \approx b'' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R' \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \approx {\uparrow}^{A''}(b'') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R'}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &b \approx b'' \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by transitivity of $\textsf{Ne}$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A''}(b'') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Ne})} \\
    &R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu} \Leftrightarrow R'
      && \text{(hence $R \Leftrightarrow R'$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Nat}$ and $\textsc{U-Univ}$: immediate.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} $\textsc{U-Pi}$.
  The first derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A_1 \approx A_2 \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_2 \rrbracket(\rho_2, a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A_1, T_1, \rho_1) \approx \Pi(A_2, T_2, \rho_2) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  The second derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A_2 \approx A_3 \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_I' \\
     R_I' \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a \approx a' \in R_I'.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T_2 \rrbracket(\rho_2, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_3 \rrbracket(\rho_3, a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R' \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a \approx a' \in R_I'.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'))}
    {\Pi(A_2, T_2, \rho_2) \approx \Pi(A_3, T_3, \rho_3) \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R'}
  \end{mathpar}

  For (1): We construct a \textsc{U-Pi} derivation of
  $\Pi(A_1, T_1, \rho_1) \approx \Pi(A_3, T_3, \rho_3) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.

  \emph{Premise 1} (domain):
  \begin{align*}
    &R_I \Leftrightarrow R_I'
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}: both have left type $A_2$)} \\
    &A_1 \approx A_3 \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I
      && \text{(by IH (1) on domain)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Premise 2}: $R_I$ is a PER (by hypothesis).

  \emph{Premise 3} (codomain): Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$.
  We must show $\ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_3 \rrbracket(\rho_3, a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$
  for some $R_O''$.
  \begin{align*}
    &a \approx a \in R_I
      && \text{(by symmetry + transitivity of $R_I$; let this be $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_2 \rrbracket(\rho_2, a/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(from first codomain at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1$)} \\
    &a \approx a' \in R_I'
      && \text{(by $R_I \Leftrightarrow R_I'$; let evidence in $R_I'$ be $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_2 \rrbracket(\rho_2, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_3 \rrbracket(\rho_3, a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_O'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(from second codomain at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T_3 \rrbracket(\rho_3, a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(by IH (1) on codomain)}
  \end{align*}
  Set $R_O''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) := R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)$.

  \emph{Premise 4} (biconditional): We must show
  $f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
  (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\; f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))$.
  Since $R_O''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) = R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)$ and by right irrelevance $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$
  (both have the same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)}$), the right-hand side is equivalent
  to the original biconditional for $R$.  Hence the same $R$ works.
  \begin{align*}
    &\Pi(A_1, T_1, \rho_1) \approx \Pi(A_3, T_3, \rho_3) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Pi})}
  \end{align*}

  For (2): Suppose $f_1 \approx f_2 \in R$ and $f_2 \approx f_3 \in R$.
  We must show $f_1 \approx f_3 \in R$, i.e.\ for all $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$,
  $f_1 \cdot a \approx f_3 \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &a \approx a \in R_I
      && \text{(by symmetry + transitivity of $R_I$; let this be $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1$)} \\
    &f_1 \cdot a \approx f_2 \cdot a \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(from $f_1 \approx f_2 \in R$ at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1$)} \\
    &f_2 \cdot a \approx f_3 \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(from $f_2 \approx f_3 \in R$ at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$)} \\
    &R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}: same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket T_1 \rrbracket(\rho_1, a/x)}$)} \\
    &f_1 \cdot a \approx f_2 \cdot a \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1) \Leftrightarrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$)} \\
    &f_1 \cdot a \approx f_3 \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by IH (2) on $R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$: transitivity)}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{lem:subty-respects}
  If $A \mathrel{<:_i} A'$, $A \approx B \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, and
  $A' \approx B' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R'$, then
  $a \approx a' \in R$ implies $a \approx a' \in R'$.
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation of $A \mathrel{<:_i} A'$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \mathrel{<:_i} {\uparrow}^{A'}(b')}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &e \approx e \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by symmetry + transitivity of $\textsf{Ne}$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{U_i}(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{U_i}(e) \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      \text{ with } R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Ne})} \\
    &e' \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by symmetry + transitivity of $\textsf{Ne}$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{U_i}(e') \approx {\uparrow}^{U_i}(e') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R'
      \text{ with } R' \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Ne})} \\
    &R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu} \Leftrightarrow R'
      && \text{(hence $R \subseteq R'$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Univ}]
    {j \le k \\ k < i}
    {U_j \mathrel{<:_i} U_k}
  \end{mathpar}
  \begin{align*}
    &U_j \approx U_j \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R
      \text{ with } R \Leftrightarrow (\lambda a\,a'.\, \exists R.\, a \approx a' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R)
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Univ}, $j < i$)} \\
    &U_k \approx U_k \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R'
      \text{ with } R' \Leftrightarrow (\lambda a\,a'.\, \exists R.\, a \approx a' \in \mathcal{U}_k \searrow R)
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Univ}, $k < i$)} \\
    &R \subseteq R'
      && \text{(by cumulativity, \Cref{lem:cumul}, since $j \le k$)}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Nat}]
    { }
    {N \mathrel{<:_i} N}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both sides are in $\mathcal{U}_i$ (via \textsc{U-Nat}) returning $\textsf{Nat}$,
  and $\textsf{Nat} \subseteq \textsf{Nat}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Pi}]
    {A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \\\\
     \Pi(A, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A, T, \rho) \in \mathcal{U}_i \\
     \Pi(A', T', \rho') \approx \Pi(A', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i}
    {\Pi(A, T, \rho) \mathrel{<:_i} \Pi(A', T', \rho')}
  \end{mathpar}
  The domain PERs coincide by hypothesis.  For the function PERs:
  \begin{align*}
    &\text{Given } f \approx f' \in R
      && \text{(i.e., $\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$)} \\
    &\text{Given } \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I \\
    &f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by above)} \\
    &R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \subseteq R_{O'}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by IH on codomain subtyping)} \\
    &f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_{O'}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by inclusion)}
  \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-51: body_md -->
\label{lem:subty-trans}
  If $A \mathrel{<:_i} B$ and $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$, then $A \mathrel{<:_i} C$.
<!-- end lemma-51 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation of $A \mathrel{<:_i} B$, with case
  analysis on the constructor of $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$ that must agree on
  the shape of $B$.  

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne}}
    {{\uparrow}^{A_0}(b) \mathrel{<:_i} {\uparrow}^{B_0}(b')}
  \end{mathpar}
  Here $B = {\uparrow}^{B_0}(b')$, so $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$ must also be by
  \textsc{$<$:-Ne}, with $C = {\uparrow}^{C_0}(b'')$ and $b' \approx b''
  \in \textsf{Ne}$.  
  By transitivity of the neutral PER (\Cref{lem:base-per}),
  $b \approx b'' \in \textsf{Ne}$.  
  By \textsc{$<$:-Ne},
  ${\uparrow}^{A_0}(b) \mathrel{<:_i} {\uparrow}^{C_0}(b'')$.  

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Univ}]
    {j \le k \\ k < i}
    {U_j \mathrel{<:_i} U_k}
  \end{mathpar}
  Here $B = U_k$, so $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$ must be by \textsc{$<$:-Univ},
  with $C = U_{k'}$, $k \le k'$, and $k' < i$.  
  By transitivity of $\le$ on $\mathbb{N}$, $j \le k'$, and $k' < i$ by hypothesis.  
  By \textsc{$<$:-Univ}, $U_j \mathrel{<:_i} U_{k'}$.  

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Nat}]
    { }
    {N \mathrel{<:_i} N}
  \end{mathpar}
  Here $B = N$, so $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$ must be by \textsc{$<$:-Nat} with
  $C = N$.  
  By \textsc{$<$:-Nat}, $N \mathrel{<:_i} N$.  

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{$<$:-Pi}]
    {A_I \approx B_I \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T_A \rrbracket(\rho_A, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T_B \rrbracket(\rho_B, a'/x)} \\\\
     \Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \approx \Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \in \mathcal{U}_i \\
     \Pi(B_I, T_B, \rho_B) \approx \Pi(B_I, T_B, \rho_B) \in \mathcal{U}_i}
    {\Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \mathrel{<:_i} \Pi(B_I, T_B, \rho_B)}
  \end{mathpar}
  Here $B = \Pi(B_I, T_B, \rho_B)$, so $B \mathrel{<:_i} C$ must be by
  \textsc{$<$:-Pi}, with $C = \Pi(C_I, T_C, \rho_C)$ and:
  \begin{align*}
    &B_I \approx C_I \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I'
      && \text{(domain of the second derivation)} \\
    &\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a \approx a' \in R_I'.\;
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T_B \rrbracket(\rho_B, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T_C \rrbracket(\rho_C, a'/x)}
      && \text{(codomain)} \\
    &\Pi(C_I, T_C, \rho_C) \approx \Pi(C_I, T_C, \rho_C) \in \mathcal{U}_i
      && \text{(self-relatedness)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Domain.}  
  By \Cref{lem:univ-trans} applied to
  $A_I \approx B_I \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I$ and
  $B_I \approx C_I \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I'$:
  $A_I \approx C_I \in \mathcal{U}_i$, with output PER (call it
  $R_I^*$) determined up to logical equivalence by
  \Cref{lem:univ-functional}; in particular,
  $R_I^* \Leftrightarrow R_I \Leftrightarrow R_I'$.  

  \emph{Codomain.}  
  Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^* :: a \approx a' \in R_I^*$ be given.  
  By the equivalence $R_I^* \Leftrightarrow R_I$, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^*$ also witnesses
  $a \approx a' \in R_I$, and by $R_I^* \Leftrightarrow R_I'$ it also
  witnesses some $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: a \approx a' \in R_I'$.  
  Apply the codomain hypothesis of the first derivation at this $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^*$
  (used as $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ in $R_I$):
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_A \rrbracket(\rho_A, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T_B \rrbracket(\rho_B, a'/x)}
      && \text{(codomain of the first derivation)}
  \end{align*}
  Apply the codomain hypothesis of the second derivation at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_B \rrbracket(\rho_B, a'/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T_C \rrbracket(\rho_C, a''/x)}
      && \text{(codomain of the second derivation, with $a' \approx a'' \in R_I'$)}
  \end{align*}
  Since $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^*$ witnesses both pairs we have $a' = a''$ at this
  instantiation; the inductive hypothesis composes the two:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T_A \rrbracket(\rho_A, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T_C \rrbracket(\rho_C, a'/x)}
      && \text{(by IH on the codomain)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Self-relatedness.}  
  Already given: $\Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \approx \Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \in \mathcal{U}_i$
  from the first derivation and $\Pi(C_I, T_C, \rho_C) \approx \Pi(C_I,
  T_C, \rho_C) \in \mathcal{U}_i$ from the second.  

  \emph{Conclusion.}  
  By \textsc{$<$:-Pi} with the four ingredients (domain in
  $\mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I^*$, codomain pointwise subtyping at every $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^*$,
  and the two self-relatedness facts):
  \[
    \Pi(A_I, T_A, \rho_A) \mathrel{<:_i} \Pi(C_I, T_C, \rho_C). \qedhere
  \]
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-52: body_md -->
\label{lem:univ-implies-subty}
  If $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$, then $A \mathrel{<:_i} A'$.
<!-- end lemma-52 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
By induction on $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i$.
  \begin{itemize}
  \@idxitem \textsc{U-Ne}: $A = {\uparrow}^{A_0}(b)$, $A' = {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(b')$,
    $b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne}$. By \textsc{$<$:-Ne}.
  \@idxitem \textsc{U-Univ}: $A = A' = U_j$ with $j < i$. By \textsc{$<$:-Univ} with
    $j \le j$.
  \@idxitem \textsc{U-Nat}: $A = A' = N$. By \textsc{$<$:-Nat}.
  \@idxitem \textsc{U-Pi}: $A = \Pi(A_I, T, \rho)$, $A' = \Pi(A_I', T', \rho')$,
    domain $A_I \approx A_I' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I$, codomain pointwise
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i$, and
    self-relatedness of both Pi-types.
    By inner IH on the codomain $\mathcal{U}_i$-equality:
    $\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)}$.
    By \textsc{$<$:-Pi}.
  \end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{lem:realizability}
  Given $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem\label{lem:R-readback}
    (Elements of $R$ read back)\; If $a \approx a' \in R$, then
    ${\downarrow}^A(a) \approx {\downarrow}^{A'}(a') \in \textsf{Nf}$.
  \@idxitem\label{lem:ne-in-R}
    (Neutrals inhabit $R$)\; If $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$, then
    ${\uparrow}^A(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(e') \in R$.
  \@idxitem\label{lem:type-readback}
    (Types read back)\; $A \approx A' \in \textsf{Ty}$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
By simultaneous induction on the derivation of $A \approx A' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R$.
  We also need an auxiliary lemma that $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$ implies
  ${\downarrow}^N(a) \approx {\downarrow}^N(a') \in \textsf{Nf}$, which is \Cref{lem:nat-readback}.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Ne}]
    {b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne} \\ R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}}
    {{\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): Since $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$, we have $a = {\uparrow}^B(e)$ and
  $a' = {\uparrow}^{B'}(e')$ with $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$.
  Reading back ${\downarrow}^{{\uparrow}^A(b)}({\uparrow}^B(e))$ at a neutral type
  reads $e$ as a neutral (by \textsc{Rf-ne}), and both sides produce the same
  neutral normal form since $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$.

  For (2): We need ${\uparrow}^{{\uparrow}^A(b)}(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{{\uparrow}^{A'}(b')}(e') \in R$.
  Since $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$, this reduces to $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$,
  which holds by hypothesis.

  For (3): We must show ${\uparrow}^A(b) \approx {\uparrow}^{A'}(b') \in \textsf{Ty}$,
  i.e.\ reading back both sides as types produces the same result.
  Since $b \approx b' \in \textsf{Ne}$, reading both as neutrals produces the same neutral
  normal form.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Univ}]
    {j < i \\ R \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{U}_j}
    {U_j \approx U_j \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): We have $a \approx a' \in R$, i.e.\ $a \approx a' \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_0$
  for some $R_0$.  By IH (3) on the $\mathcal{U}_j$ derivation (structurally smaller since $j < i$),
  $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Ty}_j$.  Reading back ${\downarrow}^{U_j}(a)$ as a normal form
  reads $a$ as a type, hence ${\downarrow}^{U_j}(a) \approx {\downarrow}^{U_j}(a') \in \textsf{Nf}$.

  For (2): We need ${\uparrow}^{U_j}(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{U_j}(e') \in R$,
  i.e.\ ${\uparrow}^{U_j}(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{U_j}(e') \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_0$ for some $R_0$.
  \begin{align*}
    &e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by hypothesis)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{U_j}(e) \approx {\uparrow}^{U_j}(e') \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow \textsf{Neu}
      && \text{(by \textsc{U-Ne}, taking $R_0 \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Neu}$)}
  \end{align*}

  For (3): $A = A' = U_j$.  Both sides read back to $\ensuremath{\texttt{Ty}_{j}}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Nat}]
    {R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}}
    {N \approx N \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): Since $R \Leftrightarrow \textsf{Nat}$, we have $a \approx a' \in \textsf{Nat}$.
  By \Cref{lem:nat-readback}, ${\downarrow}^N(a) \approx {\downarrow}^N(a') \in \textsf{Nf}$.

  For (2): We need ${\uparrow}^N(e) \approx {\uparrow}^N(e') \in \textsf{Nat}$.
  \begin{align*}
    &e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by hypothesis)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^N(e) \approx {\uparrow}^N(e') \in \textsf{Nat}
      && \text{(by \textsc{Nat-Ne})}
  \end{align*}

  For (3): $A = A' = N$.  Both sides read back to $\ensuremath{\texttt{Nat}}$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{U-Pi}]
    {A_0 \approx A_0' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_I \\
     R_I \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, f, f'.\; f \approx f' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I.\;
        f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Pi(A_0, T, \rho) \approx \Pi(A_0', T', \rho') \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): We have $f \approx f' \in R$, i.e.\ for all $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$,
  $f \cdot a \approx f' \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  Reading back ${\downarrow}^{\Pi(A_0,T,\rho)}(f)$ at level $n$:
  \begin{align*}
    &\ell_n \approx \ell_n \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(a level variable reads back to itself)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n) \approx {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n) \in R_I
      && \text{(by IH (2) on domain)} \\
    &\text{Let } \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n :: {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n) \approx {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n) \in R_I \\
    &f \cdot {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n) \approx f' \cdot {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n) \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n)
      && \text{(from $f \approx f' \in R$ at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n)/x)} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n)/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n)
      && \text{(codomain premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n$)} \\
    &{\downarrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n)/x)}}(f \cdot {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n))
      \approx
      {\downarrow}^{\ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n)/x)}}(f' \cdot {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n))
      \in \textsf{Nf}
      && \text{(by IH (1) on codomain)}
  \end{align*}
  The readback rule for $\Pi$-types assembles these into
  $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^{\Pi(A_0,T,\rho)}(f)) \searrow \lambda x.\, w$ and
  $\textsf{R}^{\textsf{Nf}}_n({\downarrow}^{\Pi(A_0',T',\rho')}(f')) \searrow \lambda x.\, w$
  with the same body $w$.

  For (2): By the biconditional, we must show that for all $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: a \approx a' \in R_I$,
  $({\uparrow}^{\Pi(A_0,T,\rho)}(e)) \cdot a
  \approx ({\uparrow}^{\Pi(A_0',T',\rho')}(e')) \cdot a' \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\text{Let } \ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, a/x)} \searrow B \text{ and }
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', a'/x)} \searrow B' \\
    &({\uparrow}^{\Pi(A_0,T,\rho)}(e)) \cdot a = {\uparrow}^B(e \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0}(a))
      && \text{(by \textsc{app-ne})} \\
    &({\uparrow}^{\Pi(A_0',T',\rho')}(e')) \cdot a' = {\uparrow}^{B'}(e' \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0'}(a'))
      && \text{(by \textsc{app-ne})} \\
    &{\downarrow}^{A_0}(a) \approx {\downarrow}^{A_0'}(a') \in \textsf{Nf}
      && \text{(by IH (1) on domain: $a \approx a' \in R_I$)} \\
    &e \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0}(a) \approx e' \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0'}(a') \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(by $e \approx e' \in \textsf{Ne}$ and above)} \\
    &B \approx B' \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(codomain premise at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^B(e \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0}(a)) \approx
      {\uparrow}^{B'}(e' \;\$\; {\downarrow}^{A_0'}(a')) \in R_O(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by IH (2) on codomain)}
  \end{align*}

  For (3): Reading back $\Pi(A_0, T, \rho)$ as a type at level $n$:
  \begin{align*}
    &A_0 \approx A_0' \in \textsf{Ty}
      && \text{(by IH (3) on domain)} \\
    &\ell_n \approx \ell_n \in \textsf{Ne}
      && \text{(reflexivity of level variable)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n) \approx {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n) \in R_I
      && \text{(by IH (2) on domain)} \\
    &\text{Let } \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n :: {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n) \approx {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n) \in R_I \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n)/x)} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n)/x)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_O(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n)
      && \text{(codomain premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_n$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket T \rrbracket(\rho, {\uparrow}^{A_0}(\ell_n)/x)} \approx
      \ensuremath{\llbracket T' \rrbracket(\rho', {\uparrow}^{A_0'}(\ell_n)/x)} \in \textsf{Ty}
      && \text{(by IH (3) on codomain)}
  \end{align*}
  The type readback rule for $\Pi$-types reads back the domain and codomain separately;
  both agree by the above.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
\label{def:ctx-per}
  The relation $\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R$ is defined inductively:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot \approx \cdot \searrow \top}

    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R_T \\
     R_T \text{ is a PER} \\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \wedge
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma', x : S' \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  Here $\top$ is the total relation (any two environments are related),
  $\rho[\Uparrow]$ is the weakened environment (dropping the head), and $\rho(0)$ is the head value.
  The universe level $i$ at which the heads are related is implicit in the conclusion.
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
\label{def:ctx-subty}
  The relation $\Gamma <: \Gamma'$ is defined inductively:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-$<$:-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot <: \cdot}

    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-$<$:-Ext}]
    {\Gamma <: \Gamma' \\
     \Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R_T \\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \\\\
     \Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma, x : S \searrow R_1 \\
     \Gamma', x : S' \approx \Gamma', x : S' \searrow R_2}
    {\Gamma, x : S <: \Gamma', x : S'}
  \end{mathpar}
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- lemma-54: body_md -->
\label{lem:ctx-functional}
  If $\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R$ and $\Gamma \approx \Gamma'' \searrow R'$,
  then $R \Leftrightarrow R'$.
<!-- end lemma-54 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By induction on the first derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot \approx \cdot \searrow \top}
  \end{mathpar}
  The second derivation also concludes $\cdot \approx \cdot \searrow \top$,
  so $R = R' = \top$ and $\top \Leftrightarrow \top$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  The first derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R_T \\
     R_T \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \;\wedge\;
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma', x : S' \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  The second derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma \approx \Gamma'' \searrow R_T' \\
     R_T' \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T'.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S'' \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R' \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T' \;\wedge\;
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'))}
    {\Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma'', x : S'' \searrow R'}
  \end{mathpar}
  We show $R \Leftrightarrow R'$, i.e.\ $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$ iff $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  \begin{align*}
    &R_T \Leftrightarrow R_T'
      && \text{(by IH on the tails)}
  \end{align*}

  $(\Rightarrow)$: Suppose $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$.
  By the first biconditional, we obtain $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T$
  with $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T'
      && \text{(by $R_T \Leftrightarrow R_T'$; call this evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(from the first head premise at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S'' \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(from the second head premise at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}: same left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])}$)} \\
    &\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by $R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$)} \\
    &\rho \approx \rho' \in R'
      && \text{(by the second biconditional, with witness $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)}
  \end{align*}

  $(\Leftarrow)$: Symmetric, swapping the roles of the two derivations.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-55: body_md -->
\label{lem:ctx-sym}
  If $\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R$, then:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma \searrow R$, and
  \@idxitem $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$ implies $\rho' \approx \rho \in R$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-55 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot \approx \cdot \searrow \top}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both statements are immediate ($\top$ is symmetric).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma \approx \Gamma' \searrow R_T \\
     R_T \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \;\wedge\;
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma', x : S' \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  For (1): We construct a \textsc{Ctx-Ext} derivation of
  $\Gamma', x : S' \approx \Gamma, x : S \searrow R$.
  We verify each of the four premises.

  \emph{Premise 1} (tail):
  \begin{align*}
    &\Gamma' \approx \Gamma \searrow R_T
      && \text{(by IH (1) on the tail; same $R_T$ by \Cref{lem:ctx-functional})}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Premise 2}: $R_T$ is a PER (by hypothesis).

  \emph{Premise 3} (head): Given $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho' \approx \rho \in R_T$, we must show
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$
  for some $R_H'$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho \approx \rho' \in R_T
      && \text{(by IH (2) on the tail applied to $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$; call this $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)
      && \text{(from the original head premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-sym} (1); same $R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)$ returned)}
  \end{align*}
  Set $R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') := R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0)$.

  \emph{Premise 4} (biconditional): We must verify
  \[
    \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
    (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \;\wedge\;
     \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'))
  \]
  The original biconditional states:
  \[
    \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
    (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \;\wedge\;
     \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))
   \]
   $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$ already discharge.  
  Moreover $R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') = R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_0) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ by right irrelevance.
  Hence both biconditionals characterize the same $R$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\Gamma', x : S' \approx \Gamma, x : S \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{Ctx-Ext})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  For (2): Suppose $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$.
  By the biconditional, there exists $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T$
  with $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  We must show $\rho' \approx \rho \in R$, i.e.\ exhibit evidence for
  $\rho'[\Uparrow] \approx \rho[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ together with the heads being related.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho'[\Uparrow] \approx \rho[\Uparrow] \in R_T
      && \text{(by IH (2) on tail applied to $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$; call this $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$)} \\
    &\rho'(0) \approx \rho(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-sym} (2))} \\
    &R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional})} \\
    &\rho'(0) \approx \rho(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by equivalence)}
  \end{align*}
  The tail evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$ and the head relatedness $\rho'(0) \approx \rho(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$
  together witness $\rho' \approx \rho \in R$ by the biconditional.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-56: body_md -->
\label{lem:ctx-trans}
  If $\Gamma_1 \approx \Gamma_2 \searrow R$, then:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \@idxitem $\Gamma_2 \approx \Gamma_3 \searrow R'$ implies
    $\Gamma_1 \approx \Gamma_3 \searrow R$, and
  \@idxitem $\rho_1 \approx \rho_2 \in R$ and $\rho_2 \approx \rho_3 \in R$ implies
    $\rho_1 \approx \rho_3 \in R$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-56 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
By induction on the first derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot \approx \cdot \searrow \top}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both statements are immediate ($\top$ is transitive).

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  The first derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma_1 \approx \Gamma_2 \searrow R_T \\
     R_T \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S_1 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T \;\wedge\;
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}))}
    {\Gamma_1, x : S_1 \approx \Gamma_2, x : S_2 \searrow R}
  \end{mathpar}
  The second derivation is:
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-Ext}]
    {\Gamma_2 \approx \Gamma_3 \searrow R_T' \\
     R_T' \text{ is a PER} \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T'.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_3 \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}') \\\\
     \forall\, \rho, \rho'.\; \rho \approx \rho' \in R' \;\leftrightarrow\;
       (\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}' :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T' \;\wedge\;
        \rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'))}
    {\Gamma_2, x : S_2 \approx \Gamma_3, x : S_3 \searrow R'}
  \end{mathpar}

  For (1): We construct a \textsc{Ctx-Ext} derivation of
  $\Gamma_1, x : S_1 \approx \Gamma_3, x : S_3 \searrow R$.

  \emph{Premise 1} (tail):
  \begin{align*}
    &\Gamma_1 \approx \Gamma_3 \searrow R_T
      && \text{(by IH (1) on the tail)}
  \end{align*}

  \emph{Premise 2}: $R_T$ is a PER (by hypothesis).

  \emph{Premise 3} (head): Given $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T$, we must show
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_1 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_3 \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho \approx \rho \in R_T
      && \text{(by symmetry + transitivity of $R_T$)} \\
    &\text{Let } \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1 :: \rho \approx \rho \in R_T \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_1 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket(\rho)} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(from first head premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1$)} \\
    &R_T \Leftrightarrow R_T'
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional} on tails: same left context $\Gamma_2$)} \\
    &\rho \approx \rho' \in R_T'
      && \text{(from $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_T$ and $R_T \Leftrightarrow R_T'$)} \\
    &\text{Let } \ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2 :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T' \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_2 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_3 \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_j \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2)
      && \text{(from second head premise at $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2$)} \\
    &\ensuremath{\llbracket S_1 \rrbracket(\rho)} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S_3 \rrbracket(\rho')} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-trans} (1))}
  \end{align*}
  Set $R_H''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) := R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)$.

  \emph{Premise 4} (biconditional): The biconditional characterizes the same $R$.
  Since $R_T$ is a PER, the quantification ranges over the same set of pairs.
  By \Cref{lem:univ-functional}, $R_H''(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$ (both have the same
  left type $\ensuremath{\llbracket S_1 \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])}$), so the biconditional is equivalent to the original.
  \begin{align*}
    &\Gamma_1, x : S_1 \approx \Gamma_3, x : S_3 \searrow R
      && \text{(by \textsc{Ctx-Ext})}
  \end{align*}

  \medskip
  For (2): Suppose $\rho_1 \approx \rho_2 \in R$ and $\rho_2 \approx \rho_3 \in R$.
  We must show $\rho_1 \approx \rho_3 \in R$, i.e.\ exhibit
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho_1[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_3[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ with
  $\rho_1(0) \approx \rho_3(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  By the biconditional, from $\rho_1 \approx \rho_2 \in R$ we get
  $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1 :: \rho_1[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_2[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ with
  $\rho_1(0) \approx \rho_2(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)$.
  From $\rho_2 \approx \rho_3 \in R$ we get
  $\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2 :: \rho_2[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_3[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ with
  $\rho_2(0) \approx \rho_3(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2)$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho_1[\Uparrow] \approx \rho_3[\Uparrow] \in R_T
      && \text{(by IH (2) on tail; call this $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$)} \\
    &R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-functional}: same left type)} \\
    &\rho_2(0) \approx \rho_3(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(from $R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_2) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)$)} \\
    &\rho_1(0) \approx \rho_3(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1)
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:univ-trans} (2))} \\
    &\rho_1(0) \approx \rho_3(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(by $R_H(\ensuremath{\mathrm{D}}_1) \Leftrightarrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$)}
  \end{align*}
  Hence $\rho_1 \approx \rho_3 \in R$ by the biconditional (with witness $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}$).
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-57: body_md -->
\label{lem:ctx-subty-trans}
  If $\Gamma <: \Gamma'$, $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R$, and
  $\Gamma' \approx \Gamma' \searrow R'$, then
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$ implies $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
<!-- end lemma-57 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
By induction on the context subtyping derivation.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-$<$:-Emp}]
    { }
    {\cdot <: \cdot}
  \end{mathpar}
  Both $R$ and $R'$ are $\top$, so the inclusion is trivial.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case}
  \begin{mathpar}
    \inferrule[\textsc{Ctx-$<$:-Ext}]
    {\Gamma <: \Gamma' \\
     \Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R_T \\\\
     \forall\, \ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho \approx \rho' \in R_T.\;
       \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho)} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho')} \\\\
     \Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma, x : S \searrow R_1 \\
     \Gamma', x : S' \approx \Gamma', x : S' \searrow R_2}
    {\Gamma, x : S <: \Gamma', x : S'}
  \end{mathpar}
  Suppose $\rho \approx \rho' \in R$.
  By \Cref{lem:ctx-functional}, $R \Leftrightarrow R_1$
  (both derive from $\Gamma, x : S \approx \Gamma, x : S$), so $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_1$.
  We must show $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
  By \Cref{lem:ctx-functional}, $R' \Leftrightarrow R_2$, so it suffices to show
  $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_2$.

  By the biconditional of $R_1$: from $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_1$ we obtain
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: \rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ with
  $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$,
  where $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.

  By the IH on the tail: from $\rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T$ we get
  $\rho[\Uparrow] \approx \rho'[\Uparrow] \in R_T'$
  (where $R_T'$ is the tail PER of $R_2$; call this evidence $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$).

  By the subtyping premise: $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])}$.
  By the head premise of $R_2$ at $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$:
  $\ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \approx \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho'[\Uparrow])} \in \mathcal{U}_i \searrow R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$.
  \begin{align*}
    &\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})
      && \text{(from above)} \\
    &\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')
      && \text{(by \Cref{lem:subty-respects}: $\ensuremath{\llbracket S \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])} \mathrel{<:_i} \ensuremath{\llbracket S' \rrbracket(\rho[\Uparrow])}$)}
  \end{align*}
  Hence $\rho \approx \rho' \in R_2$ by the biconditional of $R_2$
  (with witness $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}'$ and head $\rho(0) \approx \rho'(0) \in R_H'(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}')$),
  and thus $\rho \approx \rho' \in R'$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-58: body_md -->
\label{lem:init-in-per}
  If $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R$, then
  ${\uparrow}^\Gamma \approx {\uparrow}^\Gamma \in R$.
<!-- end lemma-58 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
By induction on the derivation of $\Gamma \approx \Gamma \searrow R$.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Ctx-Emp}: $R = \top$, so any two environments are related.

  \medskip\noindent
  \textbf{Case} \textsc{Ctx-Ext}:
  By the biconditional, we must exhibit
  $\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}} :: {\uparrow}^\Gamma[\Uparrow] \approx {\uparrow}^\Gamma[\Uparrow] \in R_T$
  with $({\uparrow}^\Gamma)(0) \approx ({\uparrow}^\Gamma)(0) \in R_H(\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}})$.
  \begin{align*}
    &{\uparrow}^\Gamma[\Uparrow] = {\uparrow}^\Delta
      && \text{(where $\Gamma = \Delta, x : S$)} \\
    &{\uparrow}^\Delta \approx {\uparrow}^\Delta \in R_T
